5.50.m: Whatever sin belongs to defilers of cows, maidens, and brahmins, / may I be smeared with that sin if I do not return!

5.50.s:
vṛthāpākaprakartṛṇāṃ vṛthāmāṃsāśināṃ ca yat ..
tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi .. 26 ..
5.50.d:
वृथापाकप्रकर्तृणां वृथामांसाशिनां च यत् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्येऽहं नागच्छामि पुनर्यदि .. 26 ..
5.50.m: Whatever sin belongs to those who cook in vain and eat meat not consecrated, / may I be smeared with that sin if I do not return!

5.50.s:
vratabhaṃgaprakartṛṇāmanṛtau gāmināṃ ca yat ..
tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi .. .. 27 ..
5.50.d:
व्रतभंगप्रकर्तृणामनृतौ गामिनां च यत् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्येऽहं नागच्छामि पुनर्यदि .. .. 27 ..
5.50.m: Whatever sin belongs to breakers of vows and to those who approach women outside the fertile period, / may I be smeared with that sin if I do not return!

5.50.s:
paiśunyasūcakānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ śastrakarmaṇām..
tena pāpena lipye'haṃ nāgacchāmi punaryadi .. 28 ..
5.50.d:
पैशुन्यसूचकानां च यत्पापं शस्त्रकर्मणाम्..
तेन पापेन लिप्येऽहं नागच्छामि पुनर्यदि .. 28 ..
5.50.m: Whatever sin belongs to slanderers and to those who live by weapons, / may I be smeared with that sin if I do not return!"

5.50.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāharasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye kalaśeśvaramāhātmye govyāghrasaṃvādavarṇanaṃnāma pañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ.. 50 ..cha..
5.50.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीति साहरस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये कलशेश्वरमाहात्म्ये गोव्याघ्रसंवादवर्णनंनाम पञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः.. 50 ..छ..
5.50.m: Thus ends the fiftieth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Dialogue between the Cow and the Tiger," in the Kalaśeśvara-māhātmya, in the Māhātmya of the Holy Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part], in the eighty-one-thousand-verse collection of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa.

5.51.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha tācchapathāñchrutvā sa vyāghro vismayānvitaḥ ..
satyaṃ matvā punaḥ prāha nandinīṃ putravatsalām .. 1 ..
5.51.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथ ताच्छपथाञ्छ्रुत्वा स व्याघ्रो विस्मयान्वितः ..
सत्यं मत्वा पुनः प्राह नन्दिनीं पुत्रवत्सलाम् .. 1 ..
5.51.m: Sūta said: / Then, hearing those oaths, that tiger was filled with astonishment; / considering it to be the truth, he said again to Nandinī, who was fond of her son:

5.51.s:
yadyevaṃ tadgṛhaṃ gaccha vīkṣayasva nijātmajam..
sakhīnāmarpayitvātha bhūya āgamanaṃ kuru .. 2 ..
5.51.d:
यद्येवं तद्गृहं गच्छ वीक्षयस्व निजात्मजम्..
सखीनामर्पयित्वाथ भूय आगमनं कुरु .. 2 ..
5.51.m: "If it is so, then go home, behold your own offspring, / and having entrusted him to your companions, make your return again."

5.51.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti vyāghravacaḥ śrutvā suśīlā nandinī tadā ..
gatālayaṃ samuddiśya yatra bālaḥ sutaḥ sthitaḥ.. 3 ..
5.51.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
इति व्याघ्रवचः श्रुत्वा सुशीला नन्दिनी तदा ..
गतालयं समुद्दिश्य यत्र बालः सुतः स्थितः.. 3 ..
5.51.m: Sūta said: / Hearing these words of the tiger, the well-behaved Nandinī then / went towards the abode where her young son was staying.

5.51.s:
athākālāgatāṃ dṛṣṭvā mātaraṃ trastacetasam..
raṃbhamāṇāṃ samālokya vatsaḥ provāca vismayāt ..4..
5.51.d:
अथाकालागतां दृष्ट्वा मातरं त्रस्तचेतसम्..
रंभमाणां समालोक्य वत्सः प्रोवाच विस्मयात् ..4..
5.51.m: Then, seeing his mother arrived out of season with an alarmed mind, / and beholding her lowing, the calf said in wonder:

5.51.s:
kasmāt prāptāsyakāle tu kasmādudbhrāṃtamānasā ..
vāṣpaklinnamukhī kasmādvada mātardrutaṃmama .. 5 ..
5.51.d:
कस्मात् प्राप्तास्यकाले तु कस्मादुद्भ्रांतमानसा ..
वाष्पक्लिन्नमुखी कस्माद्वद मातर्द्रुतंमम .. 5 ..
5.51.m: "Why have you arrived untimely, and why is your mind distraught? / Why is your face wet with tears? Tell me quickly, O mother!"

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
yadi pṛcchasi māṃ putra stanapānaṃ samācara ..
yena tṛptasya te sarvaṃ vṛttāṃtaṃ tadvadāmyaham .. 6 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
यदि पृच्छसि मां पुत्र स्तनपानं समाचर ..
येन तृप्तस्य ते सर्वं वृत्तांतं तद्वदाम्यहम् .. 6 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / "If you ask me, son, drink from my breast, / so that, when you are satisfied, I may tell you the whole story."

5.51.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
so'pi tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pītvā kṣīraṃ yathocitam ..
āghrātaśca tayā mūrdhni tataḥ provāca satvaram .. 7 ..
5.51.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
सोऽपि तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पीत्वा क्षीरं यथोचितम् ..
आघ्रातश्च तया मूर्ध्नि ततः प्रोवाच सत्वरम् .. 7 ..
5.51.m: Sūta said: / He too, hearing her words, drank milk as was proper, / and having been sniffed on the crown of his head by her, he then said at once:

5.51.s:
sarvaṃ kīrtaya vṛttāṃtamadyāraṇyasamudbhavam ..
yena me jāyate svāsthyaṃ śrutvā mātastavāsyataḥ .. 8 ..
5.51.d:
सर्वं कीर्तय वृत्तांतमद्यारण्यसमुद्भवम् ..
येन मे जायते स्वास्थ्यं श्रुत्वा मातस्तवास्यतः .. 8 ..
5.51.m: "Recount the whole event that arose in the forest today, / so that peace of mind may arise in me after hearing it from your mouth, O mother."

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
ahaṃ gatā mahāraṇye hyadya putra yathecchayā ..
vyāghreṇāsāditā tatra bhramamāṇā itastataḥ .. 9 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
अहं गता महारण्ये ह्यद्य पुत्र यथेच्छया ..
व्याघ्रेणासादिता तत्र भ्रममाणा इतस्ततः .. 9 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / "Indeed, I went into the great forest today at will, my son; / there, wandering here and there, I was caught by a tiger.

5.51.s:
sa mayā prārthitaḥ putra bhakṣamāṇo nakhāyudhaḥ ..
śapathairāgamiṣyāmi gokule vīkṣya cātmajam..6.51.10..
5.51.d:
स मया प्रार्थितः पुत्र भक्षमाणो नखायुधः ..
शपथैरागमिष्यामि गोकुले वीक्ष्य चात्मजम्..6.51.10..
5.51.m: As he was about to eat me, that claw-armed [beast] was implored by me, my son: / 'I shall return with oaths after seeing my child in the cow-herd.'"

5.51.s:
sāhaṃ tena vinirmuktā śapathairbahubhiḥ kṛtaiḥ ..
bhūyastatraiva yāsyāmi dṛṣṭaḥ saṃbhāṣito bhavān .. 11 ..
5.51.d:
साहं तेन विनिर्मुक्ता शपथैर्बहुभिः कृतैः ..
भूयस्तत्रैव यास्यामि दृष्टः संभाषितो भवान् .. 11 ..
5.51.m: I was released by him after making many oaths. / I will go back there now that you have been seen and spoken to. 11.

5.51.s:
.. vatsa uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ tatraiva yāsyāmi yatra tvaṃ hi pragacchasi ..
ślāghyaṃ hi maraṇaṃ samyaṅmāturagre mamādhunā .. 12 ..
5.51.d:
.. वत्स उवाच .. ..
अहं तत्रैव यास्यामि यत्र त्वं हि प्रगच्छसि ..
श्लाघ्यं हि मरणं सम्यङ्मातुरग्रे ममाधुना .. 12 ..
5.51.m: The calf said: / I will go right there where you are going. / Truly, dying right before my mother is praiseworthy for me now. 12.

5.51.s:
ekākināpi martavyaṃ tvayā hīnena vai mayā ..
vināpi kṣīrapānena svalpena samayena tu .. 13 ..
5.51.d:
एकाकिनापि मर्तव्यं त्वया हीनेन वै मया ..
विनापि क्षीरपानेन स्वल्पेन समयेन तु .. 13 ..
5.51.m: Even all alone, left without you, I must die / in a very short time, deprived of milk to drink. 13.

5.51.s:
yadi mātastvayā sārdhaṃ vyāghro māṃ sūdayiṣyati ..
yā gatirmātṛbhaktānāṃ sā me nūnaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 14 ..
5.51.d:
यदि मातस्त्वया सार्धं व्याघ्रो मां सूदयिष्यति ..
या गतिर्मातृभक्तानां सा मे नूनं भविष्यति .. 14 ..
5.51.m: If, O mother, the tiger slays me along with you, / the destination of those devoted to their mother will surely be mine. 14.

5.51.s:
athavā ye tvayā tasya vihitāḥ śapathāḥ śubhe ..
te saṃtu mama tiṣṭha tvaṃ tasmādatraiva gokule .. .. 15 1.
nāsti mātṛsamo bandhurbālānāṃ kṣīrajīvinām ..
nāsti mātṛsamo nātho nāsti mātṛsamā gatiḥ .. 16 ..
5.51.d:
अथवा ये त्वया तस्य विहिताः शपथाः शुभे ..
ते संतु मम तिष्ठ त्वं तस्मादत्रैव गोकुले .. .. 15 1.
नास्ति मातृसमो बन्धुर्बालानां क्षीरजीविनाम् ..
नास्ति मातृसमो नाथो नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः .. 16 ..
5.51.m: Or else, whatever oaths were made by you to him, O auspicious one, / let them be upon me! Therefore, you stay right here in the herd. 15. / There is no kinsman equal to a mother for young ones living on milk; / there is no protector equal to a mother; there is no refuge equal to a mother. 16.

5.51.s:
nāsti mātṛsamaḥ pūjyo nāsti mātṛsamaḥ sakhā ..
nāsti mātṛsamo deva iha loke paratra ca .. 17 ..
5.51.d:
नास्ति मातृसमः पूज्यो नास्ति मातृसमः सखा ..
नास्ति मातृसमो देव इह लोके परत्र च .. 17 ..
5.51.m: There is no venerable one equal to a mother; there is no friend equal to a mother; / there is no deity equal to a mother, in this world and the next. 17.

5.51.s:
evaṃ matvā sadā mātuḥ kartavyā bhaktiruttamaiḥ ..
tamenaṃ paramaṃ dharmaṃ prajāpativinirmitam ..
anutiṣṭhaṃti ye putrāste yāṃti paramāṃ gatim .. 18 ..
5.51.d:
एवं मत्वा सदा मातुः कर्तव्या भक्तिरुत्तमैः ..
तमेनं परमं धर्मं प्रजापतिविनिर्मितम् ..
अनुतिष्ठंति ये पुत्रास्ते यांति परमां गतिम् .. 18 ..
5.51.m: Thinking thus, devotion must always be offered to a mother by the virtuous. / Those sons who practice this supreme duty ordained by Prajāpati / attain the supreme state. 18.

5.51.s:
tasmādahaṃ gamiṣyāmi tvaṃ ca tiṣṭhātra gokule ..
ātmaprāṇaistava prāṇānrakṣayiṣyāmyasaṃśayam .. 19 ..
5.51.d:
तस्मादहं गमिष्यामि त्वं च तिष्ठात्र गोकुले ..
आत्मप्राणैस्तव प्राणान्रक्षयिष्याम्यसंशयम् .. 19 ..
5.51.m: Therefore I will go, and you stay here in the herd. / I will undoubtedly preserve your life with my own life. 19.

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
mamaiva vihito mṛtyurna te putrādya vāsare ..
tatkathaṃ mama jīvaṃ tvaṃ rakṣasyasubhirātmanaḥ .. .. 6.51.20 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
ममैव विहितो मृत्युर्न ते पुत्राद्य वासरे ..
तत्कथं मम जीवं त्वं रक्षस्यसुभिरात्मनः .. .. 6.51.20 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / Death has been decreed today for me alone, not for you, O son. / So how can you protect my life with your own life? 20.

5.51.s:
apaścimamidaṃ putra mātṛsaṃdiṣṭamuttamam ..
tvayā kāryaṃ prayatnena madvākyamanutiṣṭhatā .. 21 ..
5.51.d:
अपश्चिममिदं पुत्र मातृसंदिष्टमुत्तमम् ..
त्वया कार्यं प्रयत्नेन मद्वाक्यमनुतिष्ठता .. 21 ..
5.51.m: This is my final, excellent instruction, O son, given by your mother: / you must diligently carry it out, following my words. 21.

5.51.s:
bhramamāṇo vane putra mā pramādaṃ kariṣyasi ..
lobhātsaṃjāyate nāśa ihaloke paratra ca .. 22 ..
5.51.d:
भ्रममाणो वने पुत्र मा प्रमादं करिष्यसि ..
लोभात्संजायते नाश इहलोके परत्र च .. 22 ..
5.51.m: Wandering in the forest, O son, do not be negligent. / Through greed comes destruction, in this world and the next. 22.

5.51.s:
samudramaṭavīṃ yuddhaṃ viśaṃte lobhamohitāḥ ..
iha tannāsti lobhena yatra kurvaṃti mānavāḥ .. 23 ..
5.51.d:
समुद्रमटवीं युद्धं विशंते लोभमोहिताः ..
इह तन्नास्ति लोभेन यत्र कुर्वंति मानवाः .. 23 ..
5.51.m: Deluded by greed, men enter the ocean, the wilderness, and battle. / There is nothing in this world that men do not do out of greed. 23.

5.51.s:
lobhātpramādādviśraṃbhātpuruṣo vadhyate tribhiḥ ..
tasmāllobho na kartavyo na pramādo na viśvaset .. 24 ..
5.51.d:
लोभात्प्रमादाद्विश्रंभात्पुरुषो वध्यते त्रिभिः ..
तस्माल्लोभो न कर्तव्यो न प्रमादो न विश्वसेत् .. 24 ..
5.51.m: Through greed, through negligence, and through misplaced trust, a man is slain by these three. / Therefore, one should not be greedy, nor negligent, nor should one trust [recklessly]. 24.

5.51.s:
ātmā putra tvayā rakṣyaḥ sarvadaiva praya tnataḥ ..
sarvebhyaḥ śvāpadebhyaśca bhramatā gahane vane .. 25 ..
5.51.d:
आत्मा पुत्र त्वया रक्ष्यः सर्वदैव प्रय त्नतः ..
सर्वेभ्यः श्वापदेभ्यश्च भ्रमता गहने वने .. 25 ..
5.51.m: You must always guard yourself with great care, O son, / from all beasts of prey while wandering in the dense forest. 25.

5.51.s:
viṣamasthaṃ tṛṇānnādyaṃ kathaṃcitputraka tvayā ..
naikākinā pragaṃtavyaṃ yūthaṃ tyaktvā nijaṃ kvacit .. 26 ..
5.51.d:
विषमस्थं तृणान्नाद्यं कथंचित्पुत्रक त्वया ..
नैकाकिना प्रगंतव्यं यूथं त्यक्त्वा निजं क्वचित् .. 26 ..
5.51.m: Grass growing in uneven ground must not be eaten in any way by you, my dear child. / You must never wander alone, leaving your own herd behind anywhere. 26.

5.51.s:
evaṃ saṃbhāṣya taṃ vatsamavalihya muhurmuhuḥ ..
śokena mahatāviṣṭā bāṣpavyākulalocanā .. 27 ..
5.51.d:
एवं संभाष्य तं वत्समवलिह्य मुहुर्मुहुः ..
शोकेन महताविष्टा बाष्पव्याकुललोचना .. 27 ..
5.51.m: Having spoken thus to that calf, licking him repeatedly, / overcome with great sorrow, her eyes bewildered with tears, 27.

5.51.s:
tataḥ sakhījanaṃ sarvaṃ gatā draṣṭuṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
nandinīṃ putraśokena pīḍitāṃgī suvihvalā .. 28 ..
5.51.d:
ततः सखीजनं सर्वं गता द्रष्टुं द्विजोत्तमाः ..
नन्दिनीं पुत्रशोकेन पीडितांगी सुविह्वला .. 28 ..
5.51.m: then, O best of brahmins, Nandinī went to see all the companion [cows], / her limbs tormented by grief for her son, profoundly agitated. 28.

5.51.s:
tataḥ provāca tāḥ sarvā gatvā'raṇyaṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
caraṃtīḥ svecchayā hṛṣṭā vāṃchitāni tṛṇāni tāḥ ..29 ..
5.51.d:
ततः प्रोवाच ताः सर्वा गत्वाऽरण्यं द्विजोत्तमाः ..
चरंतीः स्वेच्छया हृष्टा वांछितानि तृणानि ताः ..29 ..
5.51.m: Then, having gone into the forest, O best of brahmins, she spoke to them all / as they were grazing at will, delighted, on the grasses they desired: 29.

5.51.s:
bahule caṃpake dāme vasudhāre ghaṭasrave ..
haṃsanādi priyānaṃde śubhakṣīre mahodaye .. 6.51.30 ..
5.51.d:
बहुले चंपके दामे वसुधारे घटस्रवे ..
हंसनादि प्रियानंदे शुभक्षीरे महोदये .. 6.51.30 ..
5.51.m: “O Bahulā, Campakā, Dāmā, Vasudhārā, Ghaṭasravā, / Haṃsanādā, Priyānandā, Śubhakṣīrā, Mahodayā, 30.

5.51.s:
tathānyā dhenavo yāśca saṃsthitā gokulāṃtike ..
śṛṇvaṃtu vacanaṃ mahyaṃ kurvaṃtu ca tataḥ param ..
adyāhaṃ nijayūthasya bhramaṃtī nātidūrataḥ .. 31 ..
5.51.d:
तथान्या धेनवो याश्च संस्थिता गोकुलांतिके ..
शृण्वंतु वचनं मह्यं कुर्वंतु च ततः परम् ..
अद्याहं निजयूथस्य भ्रमंती नातिदूरतः .. 31 ..
5.51.m: and the other cows that dwell near the herd, / listen to my words, and act accordingly thereafter. / Today, wandering not very far from my herd, 31.

5.51.s:
tataśca gahanaṃ prāptā vanaṃ mānuṣavarjitam ..
vyāghreṇāsāditā tatra bhramaṃtī tṛṇavāṃchayā .. 32 ..
5.51.d:
ततश्च गहनं प्राप्ता वनं मानुषवर्जितम् ..
व्याघ्रेणासादिता तत्र भ्रमंती तृणवांछया .. 32 ..
5.51.m: I then reached a dense forest devoid of human beings. / There, wandering in search of grass, I was caught by a tiger. 32.

5.51.s:
yuṣmākaṃ darśanārthāya sutasaṃbhāṣaṇāya ca ..
saṃprāptā śapathaiḥ kṛcchrāttaṃ viśvāsya nakhāyudham .. 33 ..
5.51.d:
युष्माकं दर्शनार्थाय सुतसंभाषणाय च ..
संप्राप्ता शपथैः कृच्छ्रात्तं विश्वास्य नखायुधम् .. 33 ..
5.51.m: In order to see you and to speak with my son, / I have returned with difficulty through oaths, having gained the trust of that beast with claws for weapons. 33.

5.51.s:
dṛṣṭaḥ saṃbhāṣitaḥ putraḥ śāsitaśca mayā hi saḥ ..
adhunā bhavatīnāṃ ca pradattaḥ putrako yathā .. 34 ..
5.51.d:
दृष्टः संभाषितः पुत्रः शासितश्च मया हि सः ..
अधुना भवतीनां च प्रदत्तः पुत्रको यथा .. 34 ..
5.51.m: My son has been seen, spoken to, and instructed by me; / now this little child is entrusted to you. 34.

5.51.s:
ajñānājjñānato vāpi bhavatīnāṃ mayā kṛtam ..
yatkiṃcidduṣkṛtaṃ bhadrāstatkṣaṃtavyaṃ prasādataḥ ..35..
5.51.d:
अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानतो वापि भवतीनां मया कृतम् ..
यत्किंचिद्दुष्कृतं भद्रास्तत्क्षंतव्यं प्रसादतः ..35..
5.51.m: Whatever wrongdoing has been committed by me toward you, / through ignorance or even knowingly, O good ones, that should be forgiven in kindness. 35.

5.51.s:
anātho hyabalo dīnaḥ kṣīrapo mama bālakaḥ ..
mātṛśokābhisaṃtaptaḥ pālyaḥ sarvābhireva saḥ .. 36 ..
5.51.d:
अनाथो ह्यबलो दीनः क्षीरपो मम बालकः ..
मातृशोकाभिसंतप्तः पाल्यः सर्वाभिरेव सः .. 36 ..
5.51.m: My child is indeed helpless, weak, miserable, and dependent on milk; / scorched by grief for his mother, he must be protected by all of you. 36.

5.51.s:
bhramamāṇo'same sthāne vrajamāno'nyagokule ..
akāryeṣu ca saṃsakto nivāryaḥ sarvadā''darāt .. 37 ..
5.51.d:
भ्रममाणोऽसमे स्थाने व्रजमानोऽन्यगोकुले ..
अकार्येषु च संसक्तो निवार्यः सर्वदा'ऽदरात् .. 37 ..
5.51.m: Wandering into an uneven place, going into another herd, / or engaged in inappropriate actions, he should always be held back with care. 37.

5.51.s:
ahaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi sa vyāghro yatra saṃsthitaḥ ..
apaścimapraṇāmo'yaṃ sarvāsāṃ vihito mayā .. 38 ..
5.51.d:
अहं तत्र गमिष्यामि स व्याघ्रो यत्र संस्थितः ..
अपश्चिमप्रणामोऽयं सर्वासां विहितो मया .. 38 ..
5.51.m: I will go there where that tiger waits. / This is the final bow made by me to you all.” 38.

5.51.s:
.. dhenava ūcuḥ .. ..
na gaṃtavyaṃ tvayā tatra kathaṃcidapi naṃdini ..
āpaddharmaṃ na vetsi tvaṃ nūnaṃ yena pragacchasi .. 39 ..
5.51.d:
.. धेनव ऊचुः .. ..
न गंतव्यं त्वया तत्र कथंचिदपि नंदिनि ..
आपद्धर्मं न वेत्सि त्वं नूनं येन प्रगच्छसि .. 39 ..
5.51.m: The cows said: / “You must not go there by any means, O Nandinī! / You surely do not know the duty in emergencies, which is why you are going. 39.

5.51.s:
na narmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti na strīṣu jātirna vivāhakāle ..
prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre paṃcānṛtānyāhurapātakāni .. 6.51.40 ..
5.51.d:
न नर्मयुक्तं वचनं हिनस्ति न स्त्रीषु जातिर्न विवाहकाले ..
प्राणात्यये सर्वधनापहारे पंचानृतान्याहुरपातकानि .. 6.51.40 ..
5.51.m: Words spoken in jest do not cause ruin, nor [untruth] with women, nor at the time of marriage, / nor in danger to life, nor during the loss of all one’s wealth: they declare that five untruths are free from sin. 40.

5.51.s:
tasmāttatra na gaṃtavyaṃ doṣo nāstyatra te śubhe ..
pālayasva nijaṃ putraṃ vrajāsmābhirnijaṃ gṛham .. .. 41 ..
5.51.d:
तस्मात्तत्र न गंतव्यं दोषो नास्त्यत्र ते शुभे ..
पालयस्व निजं पुत्रं व्रजास्माभिर्निजं गृहम् .. .. 41 ..
5.51.m: Therefore you must not go there; there is no fault in you here, O auspicious one. / Protect your own son and return home with us!” 41.

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
pareṣāṃ prāṇayātrārthaṃ tatkartuṃ yujyate śubhāḥ ..
ātmaprāṇahitārthāya na sādhūnāṃ praśasyate .. 42 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
परेषां प्राणयात्रार्थं तत्कर्तुं युज्यते शुभाः ..
आत्मप्राणहितार्थाय न साधूनां प्रशस्यते .. 42 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / “O auspicious ones, it is fitting to do that for the sake of preserving the lives of others; / for the sake of one's own life, it is not commended for the virtuous. 42.

5.51.s:
satye pratiṣṭhito loko dharmaḥ satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ ..
udadhiḥ satyavākyena maryādāṃ na vilaṃghayet .. 43 ..
5.51.d:
सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितो लोको धर्मः सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः ..
उदधिः सत्यवाक्येन मर्यादां न विलंघयेत् .. 43 ..
5.51.m: The world is established on truth; dharma is established on truth. / By the word of truth, the ocean does not cross its boundary. 43.

5.51.s:
viṣṇave pṛthivīṃ dattvā baliḥ pātālamāśritaḥ ..
satyavākyaṃ samāśritya na niṣkrāmati daityapaḥ .. 44 ..
5.51.d:
विष्णवे पृथिवीं दत्त्वा बलिः पातालमाश्रितः ..
सत्यवाक्यं समाश्रित्य न निष्क्रामति दैत्यपः .. 44 ..
5.51.m: Having given the earth to Viṣṇu, Bali took refuge in Pātāla; / relying upon his word of truth, the king of Daityas does not depart [from there]. 44.

5.51.s:
yaḥ svaṃ vākyaṃ pratijñāya na karoti yathoditam ..
kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ caureṇākṛta buddhinā .. 45 ..
5.51.d:
यः स्वं वाक्यं प्रतिज्ञाय न करोति यथोदितम् ..
किं तेन न कृतं पापं चौरेणाकृत बुद्धिना .. 45 ..
5.51.m: He who, having made a pledge with his own word, does not do as declared, / what sin has not been committed by that thief of evil intent? 45.”

5.51.s:
.. sakhya ūcuḥ .. ..
tvaṃ naṃdini namaskāryā sarverapi surāsuraiḥ ..
yā tvaṃ satyapratiṣṭhārthaṃ prāṇāṃstyajasi dustyajān .. 46 ..
5.51.d:
.. सख्य ऊचुः .. ..
त्वं नंदिनि नमस्कार्या सर्वेरपि सुरासुरैः ..
या त्वं सत्यप्रतिष्ठार्थं प्राणांस्त्यजसि दुस्त्यजान् .. 46 ..
5.51.m: The companion [cows] said: / “You are to be revered, O Nandinī, by all gods and asuras, / you who, for the sake of upholding truth, are giving up life that is so hard to abandon! 46.

5.51.s:
kiṃ tvāṃ kalyāṇi vakṣyāmaḥ svayaṃ dharmārthavādinīm ..
savareṃpi guṇairyuktā nityaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitām .. 47 ..
5.51.d:
किं त्वां कल्याणि वक्ष्यामः स्वयं धर्मार्थवादिनीम् ..
सवरेंपि गुणैर्युक्ता नित्यं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठिताम् .. 47 ..
5.51.m: What shall we say to you, O blessed one, who yourself speak of dharma and right conduct, / endowed with all virtues, always established in truth? 47.

5.51.s:
tasmādgaccha mahābhāge na śocyaḥ putrakastava ..
bhavatyā yadvayaṃ proktāstatkariṣyāma eva hi .. 48 ..
5.51.d:
तस्माद्गच्छ महाभागे न शोच्यः पुत्रकस्तव ..
भवत्या यद्वयं प्रोक्तास्तत्करिष्याम एव हि .. 48 ..
5.51.m: Therefore go, O fortunate one; your little son is not to be grieved over. / What we have been told by you, that we shall certainly do. 48.

5.51.s:
etatpunarvayaṃ vidmaḥ sadā satyavatāṃ nṛṇām ..
na niṣphalaḥ kriyāraṃbhaḥ kathaṃcidapi jāyate .. 49 ..
5.51.d:
एतत्पुनर्वयं विद्मः सदा सत्यवतां नृणाम् ..
न निष्फलः क्रियारंभः कथंचिदपि जायते .. 49 ..
5.51.m: Moreover, this we know: for people who always adhere to truth, / the undertaking of an action never comes to ruin in any way.” 49.

5.51.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ saṃbhāṣya taṃ sarvaṃ naṃdinī svasakhījanam ..
prasthitā vyāghramuddiśya putraśokena pīḍitā .. 6.51.50 ..
5.51.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं संभाष्य तं सर्वं नंदिनी स्वसखीजनम् ..
प्रस्थिता व्याघ्रमुद्दिश्य पुत्रशोकेन पीडिता .. 6.51.50 ..
5.51.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus to all those companion [cows] of hers, / Nandinī set out toward the tiger, tormented by grief for her son. 50.

5.51.s:
śokāgnināpi saṃtaptā nirāśā putradarśane ..
viyuktā cakravākīva lateva patitā taroḥ .. 51 ..
5.51.d:
शोकाग्निनापि संतप्ता निराशा पुत्रदर्शने ..
वियुक्ता चक्रवाकीव लतेव पतिता तरोः .. 51 ..
5.51.m: Scorched by the fire of grief, despairing of ever seeing her son again, / like a female cakravāka bird separated [from her mate], like a creeper fallen from a tree. 51.

5.51.s:
aṃdheva dṛṣṭinirmuktā praskhalaṃtī padepade ..
vanādhidevatāḥ sarvāḥ prā'rthayacca sutārthataḥ .. 52 ..
5.51.d:
अंधेव दृष्टिनिर्मुक्ता प्रस्खलंती पदेपदे ..
वनाधिदेवताः सर्वाः प्राऽर्थयच्च सुतार्थतः .. 52 ..
5.51.m: Like a blind woman deprived of sight, stumbling at every step, / she prayed to all the presiding deities of the forest on behalf of her son:

5.51.s:
prasuptaṃ bhramamāṇaṃ vā mama putraṃ subālakam ..
vanādhidevatāḥ sarvā rakṣaṃtu vacanānmama .. 53 ..
5.51.d:
प्रसुप्तं भ्रममाणं वा मम पुत्रं सुबालकम् ..
वनाधिदेवताः सर्वा रक्षंतु वचनान्मम .. 53 ..
5.51.m: “Whether he is fast asleep or wandering about, my tender infant son— / may all the presiding deities of the forest protect him at my word!”

5.51.s:
evaṃ pralapya manasā saṃprāptā tatra yatra saḥ ..
āste visphūrjitāsyaśca tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro bhayāvahaḥ .. 54 ..
5.51.d:
एवं प्रलप्य मनसा संप्राप्ता तत्र यत्र सः ..
आस्ते विस्फूर्जितास्यश्च तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रो भयावहः .. 54 ..
5.51.m: Having thus lamented in her mind, she arrived at the place where he was— / sitting with wide-open mouth, sharp-fanged, and terrifying,

5.51.s:
vyāghraḥ kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhaśca tasyā mārgāvalokakaḥ ..
saṃraṃbhāṭopasaṃyuktaḥ sṛkkiṇī parilehayan .. 55 ..
5.51.d:
व्याघ्रः क्षुत्क्षामकण्ठश्च तस्या मार्गावलोककः ..
संरंभाटोपसंयुक्तः सृक्किणी परिलेहयन् .. 55 ..
5.51.m: the tiger, his throat emaciated by hunger, watching the path for her, / filled with furious agitation, licking his lips.

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
āgatāhaṃ mahāvyāghra satye ca śapathe sthitā ..
kuru tṛptiṃ yathākāmaṃ mama māṃsena sāṃpratam .. 56 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
आगताहं महाव्याघ्र सत्ये च शपथे स्थिता ..
कुरु तृप्तिं यथाकामं मम मांसेन सांप्रतम् .. 56 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / “I have arrived, O great tiger, remaining true to my word and oath. / Sate your hunger as you wish now with my flesh.”

5.51.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā so'pi duṣṭātmā vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ ..
satyāśayā punaḥ prāptā saṃtyajya prāṇajaṃ bhayam .. 57 ..
5.51.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा सोऽपि दुष्टात्मा वैराग्यं परमं गतः ..
सत्याशया पुनः प्राप्ता संत्यज्य प्राणजं भयम् .. 57 ..
5.51.m: Seeing her, even that evil-minded beast attained the highest dispassion: / “She has returned with truthful intent, casting aside the fear of losing her life.”

5.51.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
svāgataṃ tava kalyāṇi sudheno satyavādini ..
na hi satyavatāṃ kiṃcidaśubhaṃ vidyate kvacit .. 58 ..
5.51.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
स्वागतं तव कल्याणि सुधेनो सत्यवादिनि ..
न हि सत्यवतां किंचिदशुभं विद्यते क्वचित् .. 58 ..
5.51.m: The tiger said: / “Welcome to you, auspicious and excellent cow, who speak truth! / Indeed, nothing unfavorable ever befalls the truthful.

5.51.s:
tvayoktaṃ śapathairbhadre āgamiṣyāmyahaṃ punaḥ ..
tena me kautukaṃ jātaṃ kimeṣā prakariṣyati .. 59 ..
5.51.d:
त्वयोक्तं शपथैर्भद्रे आगमिष्याम्यहं पुनः ..
तेन मे कौतुकं जातं किमेषा प्रकरिष्यति .. 59 ..
5.51.m: You swore with oaths, O blessed one: ‘I will come back.’ / Therefore I was curious: what will she do?

5.51.s:
so'haṃ bhadre durācāro nṛśaṃso jīvaghātakaḥ ..
yāsyāmi narakaṃ ghoraṃ karmaṇānena sarvadā .. 6.51.60 ..
5.51.d:
सोऽहं भद्रे दुराचारो नृशंसो जीवघातकः ..
यास्यामि नरकं घोरं कर्मणानेन सर्वदा .. 6.51.60 ..
5.51.m: As for me, O blessed one, I am wicked, cruel, and a killer of living beings; / by this action, I will constantly go to a dreadful hell.

5.51.s:
tasmāttvaṃ me mahābhāge pāpāsyātidurātmanaḥ ..
upadeśapradānena prasādaṃ kartumarhasi .. 61 ..
5.51.d:
तस्मात्त्वं मे महाभागे पापास्यातिदुरात्मनः ..
उपदेशप्रदानेन प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि .. 61 ..
5.51.m: Therefore, O highly fortunate one, you ought to show favor to me, / an evil and exceedingly wicked soul, by granting me instruction,

5.51.s:
yena me syātparaṃ śreya iha loke paratra ca ..
na te'styaviditaṃ kiṃcitsatyācārānmatirmama .. 62 ..
5.51.d:
येन मे स्यात्परं श्रेय इह लोके परत्र च ..
न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किंचित्सत्याचारान्मतिर्मम .. 62 ..
5.51.m: whereby there may be ultimate welfare for me in this world and the next. / Nothing is unknown to you, so I think, because of your truthful conduct.

5.51.s:
tasmāttvaṃ dharmasarvasvaṃ saṃkṣepānmama kīrtaya ..
satsaṃgamaphalaṃ yena mama saṃjāyate'khilam.. 63 ..
5.51.d:
तस्मात्त्वं धर्मसर्वस्वं संक्षेपान्मम कीर्तय ..
सत्संगमफलं येन मम संजायतेऽखिलम्.. 63 ..
5.51.m: Therefore proclaim to me in brief the essence of all dharma, / so that all the fruit of association with the virtuous may arise for me.”

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
tapaḥ kṛte praśaṃsaṃti tretāyāṃ dhyānameva ca ..
dvāpare yajñayogaṃ ca dānamekaṃ kalau yuge ..
sarveṣāmeva dānānāṃ nāsti dānamataḥ param .. 64 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
तपः कृते प्रशंसंति त्रेतायां ध्यानमेव च ..
द्वापरे यज्ञयोगं च दानमेकं कलौ युगे ..
सर्वेषामेव दानानां नास्ति दानमतः परम् .. 64 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / “They praise austerity in the Kṛta age, and contemplation alone in the Tretā, / the practice of sacrifice in the Dvāpara, and gift-giving alone in the Kali age. / Among all gifts, there is no gift higher than this:

5.51.s:
carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāmabhayaṃ yaḥ prayacchati ..
sa sarvabhayanirmuktaḥ paraṃ brahmā dhigacchati .. 65 ..
5.51.d:
चराचराणां भूतानामभयं यः प्रयच्छति ..
स सर्वभयनिर्मुक्तः परं ब्रह्मा धिगच्छति .. 65 ..
5.51.m: he who grants freedom from fear to beings moving and unmoving, / freed from all fear, attains the supreme Brahman.”

5.51.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
anyeṣāṃ caiva bhūtānāṃ taddānaṃ yujyate śubhe ..
ahiṃsayā bhavedyeṣāṃ prāṇayātrānnapūrvakam .. 66 ..
5.51.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
अन्येषां चैव भूतानां तद्दानं युज्यते शुभे ..
अहिंसया भवेद्येषां प्राणयात्रान्नपूर्वकम् .. 66 ..
5.51.m: The tiger said: / “Such giving is fitting for other beings, O auspicious one, / whose livelihood through food can be accomplished without violence.

5.51.s:
na hiṃsayā vinā'smākaṃ yataḥ syātprāṇadhāraṇam ..
tasmādbrūhi mahābhāge kiñcinmama sukhāvaham ..
upadeśaṃ sudharmāya hiṃsakasyāpi dehinām .. .. 67 ..
5.51.d:
न हिंसया विनाऽस्माकं यतः स्यात्प्राणधारणम् ..
तस्माद्ब्रूहि महाभागे किञ्चिन्मम सुखावहम् ..
उपदेशं सुधर्माय हिंसकस्यापि देहिनाम् .. .. 67 ..
5.51.m: Since our sustenance of life cannot take place without violence, / therefore, O highly fortunate one, speak some advice that brings happiness to me, / for the true dharma even of one who slaughters living beings.”

5.51.s:
.. nandinyuvāca .. ..
atrāsti sumahalliṃgaṃ purā bāṇapratiṣṭhitam ..
gahane yatprabhāvena tvayā muktāsmyahaṃ dhruvam .. 68 ..
5.51.d:
.. नन्दिन्युवाच .. ..
अत्रास्ति सुमहल्लिंगं पुरा बाणप्रतिष्ठितम् ..
गहने यत्प्रभावेन त्वया मुक्तास्म्यहं ध्रुवम् .. 68 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / “There is a very great liṅga here in this thicket, installed of old by Bāṇa, / by whose power I have certainly been released by you.

5.51.s:
tasya tvaṃ prātarutthāya kuru nityaṃ pradakṣiṇām ..
praṇāmaṃ ca tataḥ siddhiṃ vāṃchitāṃ samavāpsyasi .. 69 ..
5.51.d:
तस्य त्वं प्रातरुत्थाय कुरु नित्यं प्रदक्षिणाम् ..
प्रणामं च ततः सिद्धिं वांछितां समवाप्स्यसि .. 69 ..
5.51.m: Rising early in the morning, perform circumambulation of it daily, / and bow down; then you will obtain the desired perfection.

5.51.s:
nānyasya karmaṇaḥ śaktirvidyate te nakhāyudha ..
pūjādikasya hīnatvāddhastābhyāmiti me matiḥ .. 6.51.70 ..
5.51.d:
नान्यस्य कर्मणः शक्तिर्विद्यते ते नखायुध ..
पूजादिकस्य हीनत्वाद्धस्ताभ्यामिति मे मतिः .. 6.51.70 ..
5.51.m: You have no capacity for other actions, O claw-armed one, / such as worship, because of the lack of hands: this is my opinion.”

5.51.s:
evamuktvātha sā dhenurvyāghrasyātha vanāṃtike ..
talliṃgaṃ darśayāmāsa puraḥ sthitvā dvijottamāḥ .. 71 ..
5.51.d:
एवमुक्त्वाथ सा धेनुर्व्याघ्रस्याथ वनांतिके ..
तल्लिंगं दर्शयामास पुरः स्थित्वा द्विजोत्तमाः .. 71 ..
5.51.m: Having spoken thus, O best of brahmins, the cow then, standing before him, / showed that liṅga to the tiger at the edge of the forest.

5.51.s:
so'pi saṃdarśanāttasya tatkṣaṇānmuktimāptavān ..
vyāghratvātpārthivo bhūyaḥ sa babhūva yathā purā .. 72 ..
5.51.d:
सोऽपि संदर्शनात्तस्य तत्क्षणान्मुक्तिमाप्तवान् ..
व्याघ्रत्वात्पार्थिवो भूयः स बभूव यथा पुरा .. 72 ..
5.51.m: From the darśana of it, he instantly obtained liberation / from the state of a tiger and became a king again, just as he was before.

5.51.s:
śāpaṃ durvāsasā dattaṃ rājyaṃ svaṃ sahitaiḥ sutaiḥ ..
sasmāra sa nṛpaśreṣṭhastataḥ provāca naṃdinīm .. 73 ..
5.51.d:
शापं दुर्वाससा दत्तं राज्यं स्वं सहितैः सुतैः ..
सस्मार स नृपश्रेष्ठस्ततः प्रोवाच नंदिनीम् .. 73 ..
5.51.m: That best of kings remembered the curse given by Durvāsas, / and his own kingdom together with his sons; then he spoke to Nandinī:

5.51.s:
nṛpaḥ kalaśanāmāhaṃ haihayānvayasaṃbhavaḥ ..
śapto durvāsasā pūrvaṃ kasmiṃścitkāraṇāṃtare .. 74 ..
5.51.d:
नृपः कलशनामाहं हैहयान्वयसंभवः ..
शप्तो दुर्वाससा पूर्वं कस्मिंश्चित्कारणांतरे .. 74 ..
5.51.m: “I was a king named Kalaśa, born in the lineage of the Haihayas, / cursed formerly by Durvāsas for some incidental reason.

5.51.s:
tataḥ prasāditenoktastenāhaṃ naṃdinī yadā ..
darśayiṣyati talliṃgaṃ tadā muktirbhaviṣyati .. 75 ..
5.51.d:
ततः प्रसादितेनोक्तस्तेनाहं नंदिनी यदा ..
दर्शयिष्यति तल्लिंगं तदा मुक्तिर्भविष्यति .. 75 ..
5.51.m: Then, being propitiated, he told me: ‘When Nandinī / shows you that liṅga, then your liberation will occur.’

5.51.s:
sā nūnaṃ nandinī tvaṃ hi jñātā śāpāntato mayā ..
tattvaṃ brūhi pradeśo'yaṃ katamo varadhenuke .. 76 ..
5.51.d:
सा नूनं नन्दिनी त्वं हि ज्ञाता शापान्ततो मया ..
तत्त्वं ब्रूहि प्रदेशोऽयं कतमो वरधेनुके .. 76 ..
5.51.m: Indeed, you are that Nandinī, recognized by me at the end of the curse! / Tell me truly, O excellent cow: which region is this?

5.51.s:
yena gacchāmyahaṃ bhūyaḥ svagṛhaṃ prati satvaram ..
mārgaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābhāge mānuṣaṃ prāpya kañcana ..77 .. ..
5.51.d:
येन गच्छाम्यहं भूयः स्वगृहं प्रति सत्वरम् ..
मार्गं दृष्ट्वा महाभागे मानुषं प्राप्य कञ्चन ..77 .. ..
5.51.m: so that I may quickly go back to my own home, / having seen the path and met some human being, O highly fortunate one.”

5.51.s:
.. naṃdinyuvāca .. ..
camatkārapurakṣetrametatpātakanāśanam ..
sarvatīrthamayaṃ rājansarvakāmapradāyakam .. 78 ..
5.51.d:
.. नंदिन्युवाच .. ..
चमत्कारपुरक्षेत्रमेतत्पातकनाशनम् ..
सर्वतीर्थमयं राजन्सर्वकामप्रदायकम् .. 78 ..
5.51.m: Nandinī said: / “This is the sacred field of Camatkārapura, destroyer of sins, / embodying all sacred fords, O king, and granting all desires.

5.51.s:
yadanyatra bhavecchreyo vatsareṇa tapasvinām ..
dinenaivātra tatsamyagjāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 79 ..
5.51.d:
यदन्यत्र भवेच्छ्रेयो वत्सरेण तपस्विनाम् ..
दिनेनैवात्र तत्सम्यग्जायते नात्र संशयः .. 79 ..
5.51.m: The spiritual good that accrues to ascetics in a whole year elsewhere / arises here perfectly in just a single day; there is no doubt about this.

5.51.s:
evaṃ matvā mayā liṃgaṃ snāpitaṃ payasā sadā ..
etadyūthaṃ parityajya bhaktyā pūtena cetasā .. 6.51.80 ..
5.51.d:
एवं मत्वा मया लिंगं स्नापितं पयसा सदा ..
एतद्यूथं परित्यज्य भक्त्या पूतेन चेतसा .. 6.51.80 ..
5.51.m: Knowing this, leaving this herd behind, that liṅga was constantly / bathed with milk by me with devotion and a purified mind.”

5.51.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
gaccha nandini bhadraṃ te nijaṃ prāpnuhi bālakam ..
gokulaṃ ca sakhīḥ svāśca tathānyaṃ ca suhṛjjanam .. 81 ..
5.51.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
गच्छ नन्दिनि भद्रं ते निजं प्राप्नुहि बालकम् ..
गोकुलं च सखीः स्वाश्च तथान्यं च सुहृज्जनम् .. 81 ..
5.51.m: The king said: / “Go, Nandinī, blessing be upon you! Rejoin your own calf, / the herd of cows, your own friends, and other companions.

5.51.s:
etatkṣetraṃ mayā pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mukhācchrutam ..
vāṃchitaṃ ca sadā praṣṭuṃ na ca draṣṭuṃ prapāritam .. 82 ..
5.51.d:
एतत्क्षेत्रं मया पूर्वं ब्राह्मणानां मुखाच्छ्रुतम् ..
वांछितं च सदा प्रष्टुं न च द्रष्टुं प्रपारितम् .. 82 ..
5.51.m: This sacred field was heard of by me in the past from the mouths of brahmins, / and was always desired to be sought out, but I was unable to see it.

5.51.s:
rājyakarmaprasaktena bhogāsaktena naṃdini ..
svayamevādhunā labdhaṃ nāhaṃ santyaktumutsahe .. 83 ..
5.51.d:
राज्यकर्मप्रसक्तेन भोगासक्तेन नंदिनि ..
स्वयमेवाधुना लब्धं नाहं सन्त्यक्तुमुत्सहे .. 83 ..
5.51.m: Addicted to the tasks of kingship and devoted to pleasures, O Nandinī, / it has now been reached by myself spontaneously; I am not inclined to leave it.

5.51.s:
diṣṭyā me muninā tena dattaḥ śāpo mahātmanā ..
kathaṃ syādanyathā prāptiḥ kṣetrasyāsya suśobhane .. .. 84 ..
5.51.d:
दिष्ट्या मे मुनिना तेन दत्तः शापो महात्मना ..
कथं स्यादन्यथा प्राप्तिः क्षेत्रस्यास्य सुशोभने .. .. 84 ..
5.51.m: Providentially, that curse was given to me by that noble sage! / Otherwise, how could this sacred field have been attained, O fair one?”

5.51.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā mahīpālo nandinīṃ tāṃ visṛjya ca ..
sthitastatraiva talliṃgaṃ dhyāyamāno divāniśam .. 85 ..
5.51.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा महीपालो नन्दिनीं तां विसृज्य च ..
स्थितस्तत्रैव तल्लिंगं ध्यायमानो दिवानिशम् .. 85 ..
5.51.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus and bid farewell to Nandinī, the ruler of the earth / remained right there, contemplating that liṅga day and night.

5.51.s:
prāsādaṃ tatkṛte mukhyaṃ vidhāyādbhutadarśanam ..
kailāsaśikharākāraṃ tapastepe tadagrataḥ .. 86 ..
5.51.d:
प्रासादं तत्कृते मुख्यं विधायाद्भुतदर्शनम् ..
कैलासशिखराकारं तपस्तेपे तदग्रतः .. 86 ..
5.51.m: Having constructed a foremost temple of wondrous appearance for it, / shaped like the peak of Kailāsa, he performed austerity in front of it.

5.51.s:
tatastasya prabhāvena svalpaireva dinairdvijāḥ ..
saṃprāptaḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ durlabhāṃ yājñikairapi .. 87 ..
5.51.d:
ततस्तस्य प्रभावेन स्वल्पैरेव दिनैर्द्विजाः ..
संप्राप्तः परमां सिद्धिं दुर्लभां याज्ञिकैरपि .. 87 ..
5.51.m: Then, through its power, in only a few days, O twice-born ones, / he attained supreme perfection, hard even for performers of sacrifices to achieve.

5.51.s:
tatra yaḥ kārtike māsi dīpakaṃ saṃprayacchati ..
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate .. 88
5.51.d:
तत्र यः कार्तिके मासि दीपकं संप्रयच्छति ..
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः शिवलोके महीयते .. 88
5.51.m: Whoever offers a lamp there in the month of Kārtika, / freed from all sins, is glorified in the world of Śiva.

5.51.s:
mārgaśīrṣe ca samprāpte gītanṛtyādikaṃ naraḥ ..
tadagre kurute bhaktyā sa gacchati parāṃ gatim .. 89 ..
5.51.d:
मार्गशीर्षे च सम्प्राप्ते गीतनृत्यादिकं नरः ..
तदग्रे कुरुते भक्त्या स गच्छति परां गतिम् .. 89 ..
5.51.m: And when the month of Mārgaśīrṣa arrives, a person who / performs singing, dancing, and the like before it with devotion goes to the supreme state.

5.51.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam ..
kalaśeśvaramāhātmyaṃ vistareṇa dvijottamāḥ .. 6.51.90 ..
5.51.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं सर्वपातकनाशनम् ..
कलशेश्वरमाहात्म्यं विस्तरेण द्विजोत्तमाः .. 6.51.90 ..
5.51.m: All this, destroying all sins, has been told to you in detail, / the māhātmya of Kalaśeśvara, O best of brahmins.

5.51.s:
bhaktyā paṭhati yaścaitacchraddhayā parayā yutaḥ ..
so'pi pāpavinirmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate .. 91 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye kalaśeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonapaṃcāśattamo' dhyāyaḥ .. 51 ..
5.51.d:
भक्त्या पठति यश्चैतच्छ्रद्धया परया युतः ..
सोऽपि पापविनिर्मुक्तः शिवलोके महीयते .. 91 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये कलशेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनपंचाशत्तमो' ध्यायः .. 51 ..
5.51.m:
Whoever recites this with devotion, endowed with supreme faith, / is also freed from sin and glorified in the world of Śiva.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Kalaśeśvara,' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.52.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
umāmaheśvarau tatra sthāpitau tena bhūbhujā ..
prāsādaṃ paramaṃ kṛtvā sādhudṛṣṭisukhapradam .. 1 ..
5.52.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
उमामहेश्वरौ तत्र स्थापितौ तेन भूभुजा ..
प्रासादं परमं कृत्वा साधुदृष्टिसुखप्रदम् .. 1 ..
5.52.m: Sūta said: / Umā and Maheśvara were installed there by that king, / who built a supreme temple that brought delight to the eyes of good people.

5.52.s:
tasyāgrataḥ śubhaṃ kuṃḍaṃ tatra caiva vinirmitam ..
svacchodakena sampūrṇaṃ padminīkhaṃḍamaṃḍitam .. 2 ..
5.52.d:
तस्याग्रतः शुभं कुंडं तत्र चैव विनिर्मितम् ..
स्वच्छोदकेन सम्पूर्णं पद्मिनीखंडमंडितम् .. 2 ..
5.52.m: In front of it, an auspicious pool was also constructed there, / filled with clear water and adorned with clusters of lotuses.

5.52.s:
snātvā tatra naro bhaktyā tau paśyedyaḥ samāhitaḥ ..
māghaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ na sa bhūyo'tra jāyate .. 3 ..
5.52.d:
स्नात्वा तत्र नरो भक्त्या तौ पश्येद्यः समाहितः ..
माघशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां न स भूयोऽत्र जायते .. 3 ..
5.52.m: A man who bathes there with devotion and beholds the two with a concentrated mind / on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha is not born here again.

5.52.s:
tasyaiva pūrvadigbhāge'gastyakuṇḍasamīpataḥ ..
asti vāpī mahāpuṇyā sarvapātakanāśinī .. 4 ..
5.52.d:
तस्यैव पूर्वदिग्भागेऽगस्त्यकुण्डसमीपतः ..
अस्ति वापी महापुण्या सर्वपातकनाशिनी .. 4 ..
5.52.m: To the east of it, near Agastya's pool, / there is a very sacred step-well that destroys all sins.

5.52.s:
tasyāṃ yaḥ kurute snānaṃ māsi vai phālgune naraḥ ..
sopavāsaḥ sitāṣṭamyāṃ vāṃchitaṃ labhate ca saḥ .. 5 ..
5.52.d:
तस्यां यः कुरुते स्नानं मासि वै फाल्गुने नरः ..
सोपवासः सिताष्टम्यां वांछितं लभते च सः .. 5 ..
5.52.m: The man who takes a ritual ablution in it in the month of Phālguna, / fasting on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, obtains his desired wish.

5.52.s:
tasyā dakṣiṇadigbhāge tatrāsti kapilā nadī ..
kapilo yatra saṃprāptaḥ siddhiṃ sāṃkhyasamudbhavām .. 6 ..
5.52.d:
तस्या दक्षिणदिग्भागे तत्रास्ति कपिला नदी ..
कपिलो यत्र संप्राप्तः सिद्धिं सांख्यसमुद्भवाम् .. 6 ..
5.52.m: To its south is the river Kapilā, / where Kapila attained the perfection born of Sāṃkhya.

5.52.s:
kapilāyāśca pūrveṇa siddhakṣetraṃ prakīrtitam ..
yatra siddhiṃ gatāḥ siddhāḥ purā śata sahasraśaḥ .. 7 ..
5.52.d:
कपिलायाश्च पूर्वेण सिद्धक्षेत्रं प्रकीर्तितम् ..
यत्र सिद्धिं गताः सिद्धाः पुरा शत सहस्रशः .. 7 ..
5.52.m: East of the Kapilā is the celebrated Siddhakṣetra, / where formerly hundreds and thousands of perfected beings attained perfection.

5.52.s:
yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tapastatra samācaret ..
ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare nūnaṃ sa tamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 8 ..
5.52.d:
यो यं काममभिध्याय तपस्तत्र समाचरेत् ..
षण्मासाभ्यंतरे नूनं स तमाप्नोति मानवः .. 8 ..
5.52.m: Whatever desire a man contemplates when performing austerity there, / he certainly attains it within six months.

5.52.s:
tasyādhastācchilā viprā vidyate vaiṣṇavī śubhā ..
bhramantī caturasrā ca sarvapātakanāśinī .. 9 ..
5.52.d:
तस्याधस्ताच्छिला विप्रा विद्यते वैष्णवी शुभा ..
भ्रमन्ती चतुरस्रा च सर्वपातकनाशिनी .. 9 ..
5.52.m: Beneath it, O brahmins, is an auspicious, four-sided Vaiṣṇava slab / that turns, destroying all sins.

5.52.s:
sadā mahānadītoyakṣālitā muktidā nṛṇām ..
gaṃgāyamunayormadhye saṃniviṣṭā sarasvatī .. 6.52.10 ..
5.52.d:
सदा महानदीतोयक्षालिता मुक्तिदा नृणाम् ..
गंगायमुनयोर्मध्ये संनिविष्टा सरस्वती .. 6.52.10 ..
5.52.m: Constantly washed by the water of the great river, it bestows liberation on human beings. / Sarasvatī is situated between Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

5.52.s:
triveṇī vahate tasyāḥ purato bhuktimuktidā ..
tasyāmupari dagdhānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 11 ..
5.52.d:
त्रिवेणी वहते तस्याः पुरतो भुक्तिमुक्तिदा ..
तस्यामुपरि दग्धानां ब्राह्मणानां विशेषतः .. 11 ..
5.52.m: The Triveṇī flows before it, bestowing enjoyment and liberation. / For the brahmins who are cremated above it, in particular,

5.52.s:
nūnaṃ muktirbhavetteṣāṃ citā bhasmani goṣpadam ..
dṛśyate tatra tajjñātvā saṃskāryā brāhmaṇā mṛtāḥ .. 12 ..
5.52.d:
नूनं मुक्तिर्भवेत्तेषां चिता भस्मनि गोष्पदम् ..
दृश्यते तत्र तज्ज्ञात्वा संस्कार्या ब्राह्मणा मृताः .. 12 ..
5.52.m: liberation is certain. A cow's hoofprint is seen there in the funeral pyre's ashes; / knowing that, deceased brahmins should be given the funeral rites [there].

5.52.s:
tasyaivottaradigbhāge rudrakoṭirdvijottamāḥ ..
asti saṃpūjitā viprai rdākṣiṇātyairmahātmabhiḥ .. 13 ..
5.52.d:
तस्यैवोत्तरदिग्भागे रुद्रकोटिर्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
अस्ति संपूजिता विप्रै र्दाक्षिणात्यैर्महात्मभिः .. 13 ..
5.52.m: To its north, O best of brahmins, / is Rudrakoṭi, worshipped by high-souled southern brahmins.

5.52.s:
mahāyogisvarūpeṇa dākṣiṇātyā dvijottamāḥ ..
camatkārapure kṣetre śrutvā svayamumāpatim .. 14 ..
5.52.d:
महायोगिस्वरूपेण दाक्षिणात्या द्विजोत्तमाः ..
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे श्रुत्वा स्वयमुमापतिम् .. 14 ..
5.52.m: Hearing that the Lord of Umā was personally present in the sacred field of Camatkārapura / in the form of a great yogin, the best of southern brahmins,

5.52.s:
tataḥ kautūhalāviṣṭāḥ śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ ..
koṭisaṃkhyā drutaṃ jagmustasya darśanavāṃchayā .. 15 ..
5.52.d:
ततः कौतूहलाविष्टाः श्रद्धया परया युताः ..
कोटिसंख्या द्रुतं जग्मुस्तस्य दर्शनवांछया .. 15 ..
5.52.m: filled with wonder and endowed with supreme faith, / went swiftly by the crore, wishing to have his darśana.

5.52.s:
ahaṃpūrvamahaṃpūrvaṃ vīkṣayiṣyāmi taṃ haram ..
iti śraddhāsamo petāścakruste śapathaṃ gatāḥ .. 16 ..
5.52.d:
अहंपूर्वमहंपूर्वं वीक्षयिष्यामि तं हरम् ..
इति श्रद्धासमो पेताश्चक्रुस्ते शपथं गताः .. 16 ..
5.52.m: 'I will see Hara first! I will see him first!' / Having arrived, full of faith, they swore an oath:

5.52.s:
eteṣāṃ madhyato yastaṃ mahāyoginamīśvaram ..
caramaṃ devamīkṣeta bhaviṣyati sa pāpakṛt .. 17 ..
5.52.d:
एतेषां मध्यतो यस्तं महायोगिनमीश्वरम् ..
चरमं देवमीक्षेत भविष्यति स पापकृत् .. 17 ..
5.52.m: 'Whoever among us sees that great yogin, the Lord, / the God, last, will become a sinner.'

5.52.s:
tatasteṣāmabhiprāyaṃ jñātvā devo maheśvaraḥ ..
bhaktiprīto hitārthāya koṭirūpairvyavasthitaḥ .. 18 ..
5.52.d:
ततस्तेषामभिप्रायं ज्ञात्वा देवो महेश्वरः ..
भक्तिप्रीतो हितार्थाय कोटिरूपैर्व्यवस्थितः .. 18 ..
5.52.m: Then, knowing their intention, the divine Maheśvara, / pleased with their devotion, assumed ten million forms for their welfare.

5.52.s:
helayā darśanaṃ prāptaḥ sarveṣāṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
tataḥ prabhṛti tatsthānaṃ rudrakoṭītiviśrutam .. 19 ..
5.52.d:
हेलया दर्शनं प्राप्तः सर्वेषां द्विजसत्तमाः ..
ततः प्रभृति तत्स्थानं रुद्रकोटीतिविश्रुतम् .. 19 ..
5.52.m: Effortlessly, he granted darśana to all, O best of brahmins. / From that time on, that place became renowned as Rudrakoṭi.

5.52.s:
tadarthaṃ paṭhitaḥ śloko nāradena purā dvijāḥ ..
rudrāvartaṃ samālokya prahṛṣṭena dvijottamāḥ .. 6.52.20 ..
5.52.d:
तदर्थं पठितः श्लोको नारदेन पुरा द्विजाः ..
रुद्रावर्तं समालोक्य प्रहृष्टेन द्विजोत्तमाः .. 6.52.20 ..
5.52.m: For that reason, a verse was recited in ancient times by Nārada, O brahmins; / gazing upon Rudrāvarta, delighted, O best of brahmins:

5.52.s:
āṣāḍhīṃ kārtikīṃ māghīṃ tathā caitrasamudbhavām ..
dhanyāḥ pṛthivyāṃ lapsyaṃte rudrāvarte caturdaśīm .. 21 ..
5.52.d:
आषाढीं कार्तिकीं माघीं तथा चैत्रसमुद्भवाम् ..
धन्याः पृथिव्यां लप्स्यंते रुद्रावर्ते चतुर्दशीम् .. 21 ..
5.52.m: 'Blessed on earth are those who will obtain the fourteenth day [of the fortnight] / in Āṣāḍha, Kārttika, Māgha, and also that arising in Caitra, at Rudrāvarta.

5.52.s:
ājanmaśatasāhasraṃ kṛtvā pāpaṃ naraḥ kṣitau ..
rudrāvartaṃ samālokya vipāpmatvaṃ prapadyate .. 22 ..
5.52.d:
आजन्मशतसाहस्रं कृत्वा पापं नरः क्षितौ ..
रुद्रावर्तं समालोक्य विपाप्मत्वं प्रपद्यते .. 22 ..
5.52.m: Having committed sins through hundreds of thousands of lifetimes on earth, / a person becomes free from sin upon seeing Rudrāvarta.

5.52.s:
rudrāvartte naro gatvā dṛṣṭvā yogeśvaraṃ haram ..
śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ vipāpmā jāyate dhruvam .. 23 ..
5.52.d:
रुद्रावर्त्ते नरो गत्वा दृष्ट्वा योगेश्वरं हरम् ..
शुक्लपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां विपाप्मा जायते ध्रुवम् .. 23 ..
5.52.m: Going to Rudrāvarta and seeing Hara, the Lord of Yoga, / on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, a man certainly becomes free from sin.

5.52.s:
yastatra kurute śrāddhaṃ mahāyogipure dvijāḥ ..
rudrāvarte sa cāpnoti phalaṃ śatamakhodbhavam .. 24 ..
5.52.d:
यस्तत्र कुरुते श्राद्धं महायोगिपुरे द्विजाः ..
रुद्रावर्ते स चाप्नोति फलं शतमखोद्भवम् .. 24 ..
5.52.m: Whoever performs a śrāddha there at Mahāyogipura, O brahmins, / at Rudrāvarta, attains the fruit of performing a hundred horse-sacrifices.

5.52.s:
upavāsaparo bhūtvā yaḥ kuryādrātrijāgaram ..
kāmagena vimānena sa svarge yāti mānavaḥ .. 25 ..
5.52.d:
उपवासपरो भूत्वा यः कुर्याद्रात्रिजागरम् ..
कामगेन विमानेन स स्वर्गे याति मानवः .. 25 ..
5.52.m: A man who devotes himself to fasting and keeps a vigil through the night / goes to heaven in an aerial chariot that travels at will.

5.52.s:
tatra yaḥ kapilāṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye ..
sa gaṇaḥ syānna saṃdeho harasya dayitastathā .. 26 ..
5.52.d:
तत्र यः कपिलां दद्याद्ब्राह्मणायाहिताग्नये ..
स गणः स्यान्न संदेहो हरस्य दयितस्तथा .. 26 ..
5.52.m: Whoever gives a tawny cow there to a brahmin who maintains the sacred fire / becomes a gaṇa and a beloved [attendant] of Hara—of this there is no doubt.

5.52.s:
ṣaḍakṣaraṃ japedyastu mahāyogipuraḥ sthitaḥ ..
maṃtraṃ tasya bhavecchreyaḥ ṣaṅguṇaṃ rājasūyataḥ .. 27 ..
5.52.d:
षडक्षरं जपेद्यस्तु महायोगिपुरः स्थितः ..
मंत्रं तस्य भवेच्छ्रेयः षङ्गुणं राजसूयतः .. 27 ..
5.52.m: Whoever stands before the Great Yogin and recites the six-syllable mantra / obtains six times the merit of a Rājasūya sacrifice.

5.52.s:
yastasya purato bhaktyā japedvā śatarudriyam ..
caturṇāmapi vedānāṃ so'dhītānāṃ bhajetphalam .. 28 ..
5.52.d:
यस्तस्य पुरतो भक्त्या जपेद्वा शतरुद्रियम् ..
चतुर्णामपि वेदानां सोऽधीतानां भजेत्फलम् .. 28 ..
5.52.m: Or whoever recites the Śatarudriya before him with devotion / enjoys the fruit of having studied all four Vedas.

5.52.s:
gītaṃ vā yadi vā nṛtyaṃ tatpuraḥ kurute naraḥ ..
sa sarveṣāṃ bhajecchreyo makhānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..29..
5.52.d:
गीतं वा यदि वा नृत्यं तत्पुरः कुरुते नरः ..
स सर्वेषां भजेच्छ्रेयो मखानां नात्र संशयः ..29..
5.52.m: If a man performs singing or dancing before him, / he enjoys the merit of all sacrifices; there is no doubt of this.'

5.52.s:
evamuktvā dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ sa munirbrahmasaṃbhavaḥ ..
virarāma tato hṛṣṭastīrthayātrāṃ gato drutam .. 6.52.30 ..
5.52.d:
एवमुक्त्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठाः स मुनिर्ब्रह्मसंभवः ..
विरराम ततो हृष्टस्तीर्थयात्रां गतो द्रुतम् .. 6.52.30 ..
5.52.m: Having spoken thus, O best of brahmins, that sage born of Brahmā / fell silent; then, overjoyed, he quickly departed on his pilgrimage to sacred fords.

5.52.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṃḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye rudrakoṭimāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvipañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 92 .. .. cha .. .. ..
5.52.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखंडे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये रुद्रकोटिमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्विपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः .. 92 .. .. छ .. .. ..
5.52.m: Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Rudrakoṭi,' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.53.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatraivojjayanīpīṭhamasti kāmapradaṃ nṛṇām ..
prabhūtāścaryasaṃyuktaṃ bahusiddhaniṣevitam .. 1 ..
5.53.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तत्रैवोज्जयनीपीठमस्ति कामप्रदं नृणाम् ..
प्रभूताश्चर्यसंयुक्तं बहुसिद्धनिषेवितम् .. 1 ..
5.53.m: Sūta said: / Right there is the seat of Ujjayanī, granting the desires of human beings, / endowed with great wonders and resorted to by many perfected beings,

5.53.s:
yasya madhyagato nityaṃ svayameva maheśvaraḥ ..
mahākālasvarūpeṇa sa tiṣṭhati dvijottamāḥ .. 2 ..
5.53.d:
यस्य मध्यगतो नित्यं स्वयमेव महेश्वरः ..
महाकालस्वरूपेण स तिष्ठति द्विजोत्तमाः .. 2 ..
5.53.m: within which Maheśvara himself eternally resides, / in the form of Mahākāla, O best of brahmins.

5.53.s:
vaiśākhyāṃ yo narastatra kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ samāhitaḥ ..
tataḥ paśyati deveśaṃ mahākāla iti smṛtam..
pūjayeddakṣiṇāṃ mūrtiṃ samāśritya dvijottamāḥ .. 3 ..
5.53.d:
वैशाख्यां यो नरस्तत्र कृत्वा श्राद्धं समाहितः ..
ततः पश्यति देवेशं महाकाल इति स्मृतम्..
पूजयेद्दक्षिणां मूर्तिं समाश्रित्य द्विजोत्तमाः .. 3 ..
5.53.m: A man who performs a śrāddha there with a concentrated mind on the full-moon day of Vaiśākha, / and then beholds the Lord of Gods, known as Mahākāla, / should worship him, taking recourse to the southern form, O best of brahmins.

5.53.s:
daśa pūrvāndaśātītānātmānaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ ..
puruṣānsa samuddhṛtya śivaloke mahīyate .. 4 ..
5.53.d:
दश पूर्वान्दशातीतानात्मानं च द्विजोत्तमाः ..
पुरुषान्स समुद्धृत्य शिवलोके महीयते .. 4 ..
5.53.m: Raising up ten generations before and ten past, and himself, O best of brahmins, / twenty-one persons in all, he is glorified in the world of Śiva.

5.53.s:
yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāya tatra pīṭhaṃ prapūjayet ..
saṃpūjya yoginīvṛṃdaṃ kanyakāvṛndameva ca .. 5 ..
5.53.d:
यो यं काममभिध्याय तत्र पीठं प्रपूजयेत् ..
संपूज्य योगिनीवृंदं कन्यकावृन्दमेव च .. 5 ..
5.53.m: Whatever desire one contemplates when worshiping that seat, / after worshiping the host of yoginīs and the host of young girls,

5.53.s:
sa tatkṛtsnamavāpnoti yadapi syātsudurlabham ..
tatra vaiśākhamāsasya paurṇamāsyāṃ samāhitaḥ .. 6 ..
5.53.d:
स तत्कृत्स्नमवाप्नोति यदपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभम् ..
तत्र वैशाखमासस्य पौर्णमास्यां समाहितः .. 6 ..
5.53.m: one obtains all of it, even if it should be very difficult to attain. / There, on the full-moon day of the month of Vaiśākha, with a concentrated mind,

5.53.s:
śraddhāyukto naro yo vā upavāsaparaḥ śuciḥ ..
karoti jāgaraṃ tasya purataḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam .. 7 ..
5.53.d:
श्रद्धायुक्तो नरो यो वा उपवासपरः शुचिः ..
करोति जागरं तस्य पुरतः श्रद्धयान्वितः ..
स याति परमं स्थानं जरामरणवर्जितम् .. 7 ..
5.53.m: a man endowed with faith, intent on fasting and pure, / who keeps a vigil before him with faith, / goes to the supreme abode, free from old age and death.

5.53.s:
kiṃ vrataiḥ kiṃ vṛthā dānaiḥ kiṃ japairniyamena vā ..
mahākālasya te sarve kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm .. 8 ..
5.53.d:
किं व्रतैः किं वृथा दानैः किं जपैर्नियमेन वा ..
महाकालस्य ते सर्वे कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम् .. 8 ..
5.53.m: What use are vows? What use are futile gifts? What use are japas or restraints? / All of them are not worth a sixteenth part of Mahākāla.

5.53.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatraivāsti mahābhāgā bhrūṇagarteti viśrutā ..
gartā suvipulākārā sarvapātakanāśinī .. 9 ..
5.53.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तत्रैवास्ति महाभागा भ्रूणगर्तेति विश्रुता ..
गर्ता सुविपुलाकारा सर्वपातकनाशिनी .. 9 ..
5.53.m: Sūta said: / Right there, O fortunate ones, is a pit known as Bhrūṇagartā, / a pit of very vast dimensions, which destroys all sins.

5.53.s:
brahmahatyāvinirmuktaḥ saudāso yatra pārthivaḥ ..
strīhatyayā vinirmuktaḥ suṣeṇo vasudhādhipaḥ .. 6.53.10 ..
5.53.d:
ब्रह्महत्याविनिर्मुक्तः सौदासो यत्र पार्थिवः ..
स्त्रीहत्यया विनिर्मुक्तः सुषेणो वसुधाधिपः .. 6.53.10 ..
5.53.m: Where King Saudāsa was released from the sin of killing a brahmin, / [and] King Suṣeṇa was released from the sin of killing a woman.

5.53.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
brahmahatyā kathaṃ tasya saudāsasya mahīpateḥ ..
brahmaṇyasyāpi saṃjātā tadasmākaṃ prakīrtaya .. 11 ..
5.53.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
ब्रह्महत्या कथं तस्य सौदासस्य महीपतेः ..
ब्रह्मण्यस्यापि संजाता तदस्माकं प्रकीर्तय .. 11 ..
5.53.m: The seers said: / How did the sin of killing a brahmin come upon that king Saudāsa, / devoted though he was to brahmins? Relate that to us!

5.53.s:
śrūyate sa mahīpālo brāhmaṇānāṃ hite rataḥ ..
karmaṇā manasā vācā brahmaghnaḥ so'bhavatkatham .. 12 ..
5.53.d:
श्रूयते स महीपालो ब्राह्मणानां हिते रतः ..
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्मघ्नः सोऽभवत्कथम् .. 12 ..
5.53.m: It is heard that that ruler of the earth was intent on the welfare of brahmins / in deed, mind, and speech: how did he become a killer of brahmins?

5.53.s:
vimuktaśca kathaṃ bhūyo bhrūṇagartāmupāśritaḥ ..
sāpi gartā kathaṃ jātā sarvaṃ no vada vistarāt .. 13 ..
5.53.d:
विमुक्तश्च कथं भूयो भ्रूणगर्तामुपाश्रितः ..
सापि गर्ता कथं जाता सर्वं नो वद विस्तरात् .. 13 ..
5.53.m: And how was he released again having resorted to Bhrūṇagartā? / How did that pit itself come to be? Tell us everything in detail!

5.53.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
yadā liṃgasya pāto'bhūddevadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
tadā sa lajjayāviṣṭo liṃgābhāvāddvijottamāḥ .. 14 ..
5.53.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
यदा लिंगस्य पातोऽभूद्देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
तदा स लज्जयाविष्टो लिंगाभावाद्द्विजोत्तमाः .. 14 ..
5.53.m: Sūta said: / When the fall of the liṅga of the god of gods, the trident-bearer, occurred, / then, seized with shame because of the absence of the liṅga, O best of brahmins,

5.53.s:
kṛtvā'tivipulāṃ gartāṃ praviveśa tataḥ param ..
na kasyacittadātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa śūladhṛk .. 15 ..
5.53.d:
कृत्वाऽतिविपुलां गर्तां प्रविवेश ततः परम् ..
न कस्यचित्तदात्मानं दर्शयामास शूलधृक् .. 15 ..
5.53.m: having made a very spacious pit, he entered it thereafter. / At that time the wielder of the trident showed himself to no one.

5.53.s:
evaṃ sā tatra saṃjātā gartā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
yathā tasyāṃ vipāpmābhūtsau dāsastadvadāmyaham .. 16 ..
5.53.d:
एवं सा तत्र संजाता गर्ता ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
यथा तस्यां विपाप्माभूत्सौ दासस्तद्वदाम्यहम् .. 16 ..
5.53.m: Thus that pit came into being there, O best of brahmins. / I will relate how Saudāsa became free of sin in it.

5.53.s:
āsīnmitrasahonāma rājā paramadhārmikaḥ ..
saudāsastatsutaḥ sākṣātsūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ .. 17 ..
5.53.d:
आसीन्मित्रसहोनाम राजा परमधार्मिकः ..
सौदासस्तत्सुतः साक्षात्सूर्यवंशसमुद्भवः .. 17 ..
5.53.m: There was a king named Mitrasaha, exceedingly righteous; / his son was Saudāsa, born directly in the solar dynasty.

5.53.s:
teneṣṭaṃ vipulairyajñaiḥ suvarṇavaradakṣiṇaiḥ ..
asaṃkhyātāni dānāni pradattāni mahātmanā .. 18 ..
5.53.d:
तेनेष्टं विपुलैर्यज्ञैः सुवर्णवरदक्षिणैः ..
असंख्यातानि दानानि प्रदत्तानि महात्मना .. 18 ..
5.53.m: He sacrificed with extensive sacrifices having bountiful gifts of gold as fees; / countless gifts were bestowed by that great-souled one.

5.53.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya satre dvādaśavārṣike ..
vartamāne yathānyāyaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .. 19 ..
5.53.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके ..
वर्तमाने यथान्यायं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा .. 19 ..
5.53.m: Now after some time, while a twelve-year sacrificial session / was proceeding according to rule through rites prescribed by injunction,

5.53.s:
krūrākṣaḥ krūrabuddhiśca rākṣasau balavattarau ..
yajñavighnāya saṃprāptau saṃprāpte rajanīmukhe .. 6.53.20 ..
5.53.d:
क्रूराक्षः क्रूरबुद्धिश्च राक्षसौ बलवत्तरौ ..
यज्ञविघ्नाय संप्राप्तौ संप्राप्ते रजनीमुखे .. 6.53.20 ..
5.53.m: Krūrākṣa and Krūrabuddhi, two very powerful rākṣasas, / arrived to obstruct the sacrifice when the onset of night had arrived,

5.53.s:
rākṣasairbahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ tathānyairbhūtasaṃjñitaiḥ ..
piśācaiśca durādharṣairyajñavidhvaṃsatatparaiḥ .. 21 ..
5.53.d:
राक्षसैर्बहुभिः सार्धं तथान्यैर्भूतसंज्ञितैः ..
पिशाचैश्च दुराधर्षैर्यज्ञविध्वंसतत्परैः .. 21 ..
5.53.m: together with many rākṣasas and others called bhūtas, / and unconquerable piśācas, bent on destroying the sacrifice.

5.53.s:
atha te rākṣasāḥ sarve kiṃcicchidramavekṣya ca ..
viviśuryajñavāṭaṃ taṃ prasarpantaḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 22 ..
5.53.d:
अथ ते राक्षसाः सर्वे किंचिच्छिद्रमवेक्ष्य च ..
विविशुर्यज्ञवाटं तं प्रसर्पन्तः समंततः .. 22 ..
5.53.m: Then all those rākṣasas, having watched for some vulnerability, / entered that sacrificial enclosure, creeping in from all sides,

5.53.s:
nighnanto brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhānbhakṣayanto havīṃṣi ca ..
tathā yāni vicitrāṇi yajñārthe kalpitāni ca .. 23 ..
5.53.d:
निघ्नन्तो ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठान्भक्षयन्तो हवींषि च ..
तथा यानि विचित्राणि यज्ञार्थे कल्पितानि च .. 23 ..
5.53.m: slaying the best of brahmins and eating the oblations, / as well as whatever diverse [offerings] had been prepared for the sacrifice.

5.53.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra hāhākāro mahānabhūt ..
bhakṣyamāṇeṣu vipreṣu rākṣasairbalavattaraiḥ .. 24 ..
5.53.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र हाहाकारो महानभूत् ..
भक्ष्यमाणेषु विप्रेषु राक्षसैर्बलवत्तरैः .. 24 ..
5.53.m: At that moment a great cry of distress arose there, / as the brahmins were being devoured by the very powerful rākṣasas.

5.53.s:
tato maitrasahiḥ kruddhastyaktvā dīkṣāvrataṃ nṛpaḥ ..
ādāya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ dhvaṃsayāmāsa vīkṣya tān .. 25 ..
5.53.d:
ततो मैत्रसहिः क्रुद्धस्त्यक्त्वा दीक्षाव्रतं नृपः ..
आदाय सशरं चापं ध्वंसयामास वीक्ष्य तान् .. 25 ..
5.53.m: Then the king, the son of Mitrasaha, enraged, abandoned his rite of initiation; / taking up his bow with arrows, he saw them and destroyed them.

5.53.s:
kṛtarakṣo vasiṣṭhena svayameva purodhasā ..
krūrākṣaṃ sūdayāmāsa rākṣasairbahubhiḥ saha .. 26 ..
5.53.d:
कृतरक्षो वसिष्ठेन स्वयमेव पुरोधसा ..
क्रूराक्षं सूदयामास राक्षसैर्बहुभिः सह .. 26 ..
5.53.m: Having been protected by Vasiṣṭha himself, the family priest, / he slew Krūrākṣa along with many rākṣasas.

5.53.s:
krūrabuddhiratho vīkṣya hataṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sahodaram ..
taṃ ca pārthivaśārdūlamagamyaṃ brahmatejasā .. 27 ..
5.53.d:
क्रूरबुद्धिरथो वीक्ष्य हतं श्रेष्ठं सहोदरम् ..
तं च पार्थिवशार्दूलमगम्यं ब्रह्मतेजसा .. 27 ..
5.53.m: Then Krūrabuddhi, seeing his distinguished brother slain, / and that tiger among kings unapproachable because of his brahminic power,

5.53.s:
hataśeṣānsamādāya rākṣasānbalasaṃyutaḥ ..
palāyanaṃ bhayāccakre kṣatāṃgastasya sāyakaiḥ .. 28 ..
5.53.d:
हतशेषान्समादाय राक्षसान्बलसंयुतः ..
पलायनं भयाच्चक्रे क्षतांगस्तस्य सायकैः .. 28 ..
5.53.m: took the surviving rākṣasas and, being endowed with strength, / fled in fear, his limbs wounded by the king's arrows.

5.53.s:
tatastadvairamāśritya bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya rākṣasaḥ ..
chidramanveṣayāmāsa tadvadhāya divāniśam .. 29 ..
5.53.d:
ततस्तद्वैरमाश्रित्य भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य राक्षसः ..
छिद्रमन्वेषयामास तद्वधाय दिवानिशम् .. 29 ..
5.53.m: Then, harboring hostility on behalf of that elder brother of his, the rākṣasa / looked for an opening day and night in order to kill him.

5.53.s:
evaṃ savīkṣamāṇasya tasya cchidraṃ mahātmanaḥ ..
samāptimagamadviprāḥ satraṃ taddvādaśābdikam .. 6.53.30 ..
5.53.d:
एवं सवीक्षमाणस्य तस्य च्छिद्रं महात्मनः ..
समाप्तिमगमद्विप्राः सत्रं तद्द्वादशाब्दिकम् .. 6.53.30 ..
5.53.m: While he was thus watching for a vulnerability in that great-souled one, / that twelve-year sacrificial session came to an end, O brahmins.

5.53.s:
na sūkṣmamapi saṃprāptaṃ chidraṃ tena durātmanā ..
vasiṣṭhavihitā rakṣā satre tasya mahīpateḥ .. 31 ..
5.53.d:
न सूक्ष्ममपि संप्राप्तं छिद्रं तेन दुरात्मना ..
वसिष्ठविहिता रक्षा सत्रे तस्य महीपतेः .. 31 ..
5.53.m: Not even the slightest opening was found by that evil-minded one; / protection had been established by Vasiṣṭha at the sacrificial session of that king.

5.53.s:
athāsau brāhmaṇānsarvānvisṛjyāhitadakṣiṇān..
kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā vasiṣṭhamidamabravīt .. 32 ..
5.53.d:
अथासौ ब्राह्मणान्सर्वान्विसृज्याहितदक्षिणान्..
कृतांजलिपुटो भूत्वा वसिष्ठमिदमब्रवीत् .. 32 ..
5.53.m: Then he dismissed all the brahmins after their sacrificial fees had been given, / and with palms joined in reverence, he spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha:

5.53.s:
svahastena gurodyāhaṃ tvāṃ bhojayitumutsahe ..
kriyatāṃ tatprasādo me bhuktvādya mama mandire .. 33 ..
5.53.d:
स्वहस्तेन गुरोद्याहं त्वां भोजयितुमुत्सहे ..
क्रियतां तत्प्रसादो मे भुक्त्वाद्य मम मन्दिरे .. 33 ..
5.53.m: "O guru, today I wish to feed you with my own hand; / let that favor be done to me by dining today in my house."

5.53.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
sa tatheti pratijñāya vasiṣṭho munisattamaḥ ..
kṣālitāṃghriḥ svayaṃ tena niviṣṭo bhojanāya vai .. 34 ..
5.53.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय वसिष्ठो मुनिसत्तमः ..
क्षालितांघ्रिः स्वयं तेन निविष्टो भोजनाय वै .. 34 ..
5.53.m: Sūta said: / Agreeing with 'So be it,' Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages, / had his feet washed by the king himself and sat down indeed for the meal.

5.53.s:
kūrabuddhiratho vīkṣya tadarthaṃ cāmiṣaṃ śubham ..
susaṃskṛtaṃ vidhānena sūpakārairdvijottamāḥ ..35..
5.53.d:
कूरबुद्धिरथो वीक्ष्य तदर्थं चामिषं शुभम् ..
सुसंस्कृतं विधानेन सूपकारैर्द्विजोत्तमाः ..35..
5.53.m: Then Krūrabuddhi, seeing wholesome meat prepared for that purpose / by the cooks according to the rules, O best of brahmins,

5.53.s:
ukhāṃ kṛtvā tatastādṛktatpramāṇāmatarkitām..
mahāmāṃsābhṛtāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ jahārāmiṣānvitām ..36..
5.53.d:
उखां कृत्वा ततस्तादृक्तत्प्रमाणामतर्किताम्..
महामांसाभृतां कृत्वा तां जहारामिषान्विताम् ..36..
5.53.m: made an identical cooking-pot of that same size unobserved; / filling it with human flesh, he took away the one containing meat.

5.53.s:
athāsau muniśārdūlo bhuṃjāno bubudhe hi tat ..
mahāmāṃsamiti kruddhastatra provāca manyumān.. 37 ..
5.53.d:
अथासौ मुनिशार्दूलो भुंजानो बुबुधे हि तत् ..
महामांसमिति क्रुद्धस्तत्र प्रोवाच मन्युमान्.. 37 ..
5.53.m: Then that tiger among sages, while eating, realized it: / 'This is human flesh!' Enraged, full of wrath, he spoke there:

5.53.s:
mahāmāṃsāśanaṃ yasmātkārito'haṃ tvayādhama ..
rakṣovadrākṣasastasmāttvamadyaiva bhaviṣyasi ..38 ..
5.53.d:
महामांसाशनं यस्मात्कारितोऽहं त्वयाधम ..
रक्षोवद्राक्षसस्तस्मात्त्वमद्यैव भविष्यसि ..38 ..
5.53.m: "Because the consumption of human flesh was caused by you, O wretched one, / therefore you shall become a rākṣasa like a demon this very day!"

5.53.s:
tataḥ saṃśodhayāmāsa tasya māṃsasya cāgamam ..
nipuṇaṃ sūpakārāṃstāndṛṣṭvā rājā pṛthakpṛthak .. 39 ..
5.53.d:
ततः संशोधयामास तस्य मांसस्य चागमम् ..
निपुणं सूपकारांस्तान्दृष्ट्वा राजा पृथक्पृथक् .. 39 ..
5.53.m: Then the king thoroughly investigated the origin of that meat, / questioning those cooks individually.

5.53.s:
te'bruvannaitadasmābhiḥ śrapitaṃ māṃsamīdṛśam ..
śraddhīyatāṃ mahīpāla nānyena manujena vā .. 6.53.40 ..
5.53.d:
तेऽब्रुवन्नैतदस्माभिः श्रपितं मांसमीदृशम् ..
श्रद्धीयतां महीपाल नान्येन मनुजेन वा .. 6.53.40 ..
5.53.m: They said: "Such meat was not cooked by us, / believe it, O ruler of the earth, nor by any other human being,

5.53.s:
rākṣasaṃ vā piśācaṃ vā dānavaṃ vā vinā vibho ..
etajjñātvā tato nātha yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara .. 41 ..
5.53.d:
राक्षसं वा पिशाचं वा दानवं वा विना विभो ..
एतज्ज्ञात्वा ततो नाथ यद्युक्तं तत्समाचर .. 41 ..
5.53.m: except a rākṣasa, a piśāca, or a dānava, O lord. / Having realized this, O protector, do then whatever is fitting."

5.53.s:
etasminnaṃtare tasya nārado munisattamaḥ..
samāgatyābravītsarvaṃ tadrākṣasaviceṣṭitam.. 42 ...
5.53.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तस्य नारदो मुनिसत्तमः..
समागत्याब्रवीत्सर्वं तद्राक्षसविचेष्टितम्.. 42 ...
5.53.m: In the meantime, Nārada, the best of sages, / arrived and told him all the deeds of that rākṣasa.

5.53.s:
tacchrutvā kopamāpannaḥ sa rājā śaptumudyataḥ ..
vasiṣṭhaṃ svakare kṛtvā jalaṃ saudāsabhūpatiḥ ..
śāpodyataṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā nārado vākyamabravīt .. 43 ..
5.53.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा कोपमापन्नः स राजा शप्तुमुद्यतः ..
वसिष्ठं स्वकरे कृत्वा जलं सौदासभूपतिः ..
शापोद्यतं च तं दृष्ट्वा नारदो वाक्यमब्रवीत् .. 43 ..
5.53.m: Hearing that, the king was seized with anger and prepared to curse him; / taking water in his hand, King Saudāsa prepared to curse Vasiṣṭha; / seeing him bent on cursing, Nārada spoke these words:

5.53.s:
nighnanto vā śapanto vā dviṣanto vā dvijātayaḥ..
namaskāryā mahīpāla tathāpi svahitecchunā..
gurureṣa punarmānyastava pārthivasattama..44..
5.53.d:
निघ्नन्तो वा शपन्तो वा द्विषन्तो वा द्विजातयः..
नमस्कार्या महीपाल तथापि स्वहितेच्छुना..
गुरुरेष पुनर्मान्यस्तव पार्थिवसत्तम..44..
5.53.m: "Whether striking, cursing, or hating, the twice-born / are to be bowed to, O king, by one desiring his own welfare; / moreover, this one is your guru, worthy of honor, O best of kings.

5.53.s:
tasmānnārhasi śaptuṃ tvaṃ pratiśāpena sanmunim ..
niṣiddhaḥ sa tathā bhūpastatastatsalilaṃ karāt ..
pādayoḥ kṛtsnamupari pramumoca tataḥ param .. 45 ..
5.53.d:
तस्मान्नार्हसि शप्तुं त्वं प्रतिशापेन सन्मुनिम् ..
निषिद्धः स तथा भूपस्ततस्तत्सलिलं करात् ..
पादयोः कृत्स्नमुपरि प्रमुमोच ततः परम् .. 45 ..
5.53.m: Therefore you ought not to curse the virtuous sage with a counter-curse." / Being thus restrained, the king then poured all that water from his hand / onto his own feet.

5.53.s:
atha tau caraṇau tasya tapta śāpodakaplutau ..
dagdhau kṛṣṇatvamāpannau tatkṣaṇāddvijasattamāḥ .. 46 ..
5.53.d:
अथ तौ चरणौ तस्य तप्त शापोदकप्लुतौ ..
दग्धौ कृष्णत्वमापन्नौ तत्क्षणाद्द्विजसत्तमाः .. 46 ..
5.53.m: Then both of his feet, drenched by the heated curse-water, / were burnt and turned black that very moment, O best of brahmins.

5.53.s:
kalmāṣapāda ityuktastataḥprabhṛti sa kṣitau ..
bhūpālo dvijaśārdūlā nāmnā tena viśeṣataḥ .. 47 ..
5.53.d:
कल्माषपाद इत्युक्तस्ततःप्रभृति स क्षितौ ..
भूपालो द्विजशार्दूला नाम्ना तेन विशेषतः .. 47 ..
5.53.m: From that time forth he was called Kalmāṣapāda on earth; / that king, O tigers among brahmins, was distinguished by that name.

5.53.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etasminnaṃtare vipro vasiṣṭho lajjayānvitaḥ ..
jñātvā dattaṃ vṛthā śāpaṃ tasya bhūmipatestadā .. 48..
5.53.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे विप्रो वसिष्ठो लज्जयान्वितः ..
ज्ञात्वा दत्तं वृथा शापं तस्य भूमिपतेस्तदा .. 48..
5.53.m: Sūta said: / At that moment, the brahmin Vasiṣṭha was overcome with shame, / realizing that a curse had been given in vain to that king.

5.53.s:
uvāca vyarthaḥ śāpo'yaṃ tava datto mayā nṛpa ..
na ca me jāyate vākyamasatyaṃ hi kathaṃcana .. 49 ..
5.53.d:
उवाच व्यर्थः शापोऽयं तव दत्तो मया नृप ..
न च मे जायते वाक्यमसत्यं हि कथंचन .. 49 ..
5.53.m: He said: "This curse was given to you in vain by me, O king; / yet my word cannot ever turn out false.

5.53.s:
tasmāttvaṃ rākṣaso bhūtvā kañcitkālaṃ nṛpo ttama ..
svarūpaṃ lapsyase bhūyo yasminkāle śṛṇuṣva tam .. 6.53.50 ..
5.53.d:
तस्मात्त्वं राक्षसो भूत्वा कञ्चित्कालं नृपो त्तम ..
स्वरूपं लप्स्यसे भूयो यस्मिन्काले शृणुष्व तम् .. 6.53.50 ..
5.53.m: Therefore, having become a rākṣasa for some time, O best of kings, / you will regain your own form; listen to the time when [it will happen]:

5.53.s:
yadā tvaṃ krūrabuddhiṃ taṃ rākṣasaṃ nihaniṣyasi ..
tadā tvaṃ lapsyase mokṣaṃ rākṣasatvātsudāruṇāt .. 51 ..
5.53.d:
यदा त्वं क्रूरबुद्धिं तं राक्षसं निहनिष्यसि ..
तदा त्वं लप्स्यसे मोक्षं राक्षसत्वात्सुदारुणात् .. 51 ..
5.53.m: When you slay that rākṣasa Krūrabuddhi, / then you will attain release from that very dreadful state of being a rākṣasa."

5.53.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etasminnantare rājā yātudhāno babhūva saḥ ..
ūrdhvakeśo mahākāyaḥ kṛṣṇadanto bhayā nakaḥ .. 52 ..
5.53.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राजा यातुधानो बभूव सः ..
ऊर्ध्वकेशो महाकायः कृष्णदन्तो भया नकः .. 52 ..
5.53.m: Sūta said: / In the meantime, that king became a rakshasa, / with hair standing on end, a huge body, black teeth, and a terrifying form.

5.53.s:
tato jaghāna viprendrānrākṣasaṃ bhāvamāśritaḥ ..
yajñānvidhvaṃsayāmāsa munīnāmāśramānapi .. 53 ..
5.53.d:
ततो जघान विप्रेन्द्रान्राक्षसं भावमाश्रितः ..
यज्ञान्विध्वंसयामास मुनीनामाश्रमानपि .. 53 ..
5.53.m: Then, having assumed a demonic nature, he killed eminent brahmins; / he destroyed sacrifices and also the hermitages of sages.

5.53.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya krūra buddhiḥ sa rākṣasaḥ ..
jñātvā taṃ rākṣasībhūtamekadā''yudhavarjitam .. 54 ..
5.53.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य क्रूर बुद्धिः स राक्षसः ..
ज्ञात्वा तं राक्षसीभूतमेकदा'ऽयुधवर्जितम् .. 54 ..
5.53.m: Then, after some time, that cruel-minded rakshasa, / having learned that the king had become a rakshasa and was once unarmed,

5.53.s:
bhrāturvadhakṛtaṃ vairaṃ smaramāṇastataḥ param ..
tadvadhārthaṃ samāyāto rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtaḥ .. 55 ..
5.53.d:
भ्रातुर्वधकृतं वैरं स्मरमाणस्ततः परम् ..
तद्वधार्थं समायातो राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतः .. 55 ..
5.53.m: remembering his enmity caused by the killing of his brother, / arrived to kill him, surrounded by many rakshasas.

5.53.s:
tatastaṃ veṣṭayitvāpi samaṃtādrākṣaso nṛpam ..
provāca vacanaṃ kruddho nādenāpūrayandiśaḥ .. 56 ..
5.53.d:
ततस्तं वेष्टयित्वापि समंताद्राक्षसो नृपम् ..
प्रोवाच वचनं क्रुद्धो नादेनापूरयन्दिशः .. 56 ..
5.53.m: Then, surrounding that king on all sides, / the enraged rakshasa spoke these words, filling the quarters with his roar:

5.53.s:
tvayā yo nihato'smākaṃ jyeṣṭho bhrātā sudurmate ..
vasiṣṭhasya balādyajñe tasyādya phalamāpnuhi .. 57 ..
5.53.d:
त्वया यो निहतोऽस्माकं ज्येष्ठो भ्राता सुदुर्मते ..
वसिष्ठस्य बलाद्यज्ञे तस्याद्य फलमाप्नुहि .. 57 ..
5.53.m: "You who killed our eldest brother, O evil-minded one, / at the sacrifice by the power of Vasiṣṭha—reap the fruit of that today!"

5.53.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
yadbravīṣi durācāra karmaṇā tatsamācara ..
śāradasyeva meghasya garjitaṃ tava niṣphalam .. 58 ..
5.53.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
यद्ब्रवीषि दुराचार कर्मणा तत्समाचर ..
शारदस्येव मेघस्य गर्जितं तव निष्फलम् .. 58 ..
5.53.m: The king said: / "What you say, you wicked-mannered one, carry out by deed! / Your roar is useless, like that of an autumn cloud."

5.53.s:
evamuktvā samādāya tato vṛkṣaṃ sa pārthivaḥ ..
prādravatsaṃmukhaṃ tasya garjamāno yathā ghanaḥ ..59..
5.53.d:
एवमुक्त्वा समादाय ततो वृक्षं स पार्थिवः ..
प्राद्रवत्संमुखं तस्य गर्जमानो यथा घनः ..59..
5.53.m: Having spoken thus, the king took up a tree / and rushed toward him, roaring like a cloud.

5.53.s:
so'pi vṛkṣaṃ samutpāṭya krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ ..
triśaṃkhāṃ bhṛkuṭīṃ kṛtvā tasyāpyabhimukhaṃ yayau .. 6.53.60 ..
5.53.d:
सोऽपि वृक्षं समुत्पाट्य क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ..
त्रिशंखां भृकुटीं कृत्वा तस्याप्यभिमुखं ययौ .. 6.53.60 ..
5.53.m: He too, uprooting a tree, his eyes bloodshot with rage, / knitted his brows into three furrows and advanced against him.

5.53.s:
evaṃ dvāvapi tau śūrau vṛkṣayuddhaṃ mahābalau 0.
kṛtavantau vane tatra bahuvṛkṣakṣayāvaham .. 61 ..
5.53.d:
एवं द्वावपि तौ शूरौ वृक्षयुद्धं महाबलौ 0.
कृतवन्तौ वने तत्र बहुवृक्षक्षयावहम् .. 61 ..
5.53.m: Thus both warriors of mighty strength fought a duel with trees / in that forest, causing the destruction of many trees.

5.53.s:
atha taṃ śrāṃtamālokya kūrabuddhiṃ mahīpatiḥ ..
pragṛhya pādayorvegādbhrāmayāmāsa puṣkare .. 62 ..
5.53.d:
अथ तं श्रांतमालोक्य कूरबुद्धिं महीपतिः ..
प्रगृह्य पादयोर्वेगाद्भ्रामयामास पुष्करे .. 62 ..
5.53.m: Then, seeing that cruel-minded one exhausted, the king / seized him by the feet and swiftly whirled him through the sky.

5.53.s:
tataścāsphoṭayāmāsa bhūmau kopasamanvitaḥ ..
cakre cāmiṣakhaṇḍaṃ sa piṣṭvāpiṣṭvā muhurmuhuḥ .. 63 ..
5.53.d:
ततश्चास्फोटयामास भूमौ कोपसमन्वितः ..
चक्रे चामिषखण्डं स पिष्ट्वापिष्ट्वा मुहुर्मुहुः .. 63 ..
5.53.m: Filled with wrath, he dashed him to the ground / and reduced him to pieces of meat, crushing him again and again.

5.53.s:
tasmiṃstu nihate śūre rākṣase sa mahīpatiḥ ..
rākṣasatvādvinirmukto lebhe kāyaṃ nṛpodbhavam .. 64 ..
5.53.d:
तस्मिंस्तु निहते शूरे राक्षसे स महीपतिः ..
राक्षसत्वाद्विनिर्मुक्तो लेभे कायं नृपोद्भवम् .. 64 ..
5.53.m: When that heroic rakshasa was slain, the king, / released from rakshasa-hood, regained his royal human form.

5.53.s:
tataste rākṣasāḥ śeṣāḥ samaṃtāttaṃ mahīpatim..
parivārya mahāvṛkṣairjaghnuḥ pāṣāṇavṛṣṭibhiḥ.. 65 ..
5.53.d:
ततस्ते राक्षसाः शेषाः समंतात्तं महीपतिम्..
परिवार्य महावृक्षैर्जघ्नुः पाषाणवृष्टिभिः.. 65 ..
5.53.m: Then the remaining rakshasas surrounded that king on all sides / and struck him with huge trees and showers of stones.

5.53.s:
tatastānapi bhūpālo jaghāna prahasanniva ..
vṛkṣahastastu viśrabdho līlayā dvijasattamāḥ .. 66 ..
5.53.d:
ततस्तानपि भूपालो जघान प्रहसन्निव ..
वृक्षहस्तस्तु विश्रब्धो लीलया द्विजसत्तमाः .. 66 ..
5.53.m: Then the king, laughing as it were, / tree in hand, struck them down effortlessly with confidence, O best of brahmins.

5.53.s:
tataśca svapuraṃ prāptaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ ..
rākṣasānāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā labdhvā dehaṃ purātanam .. 67 ..
5.53.d:
ततश्च स्वपुरं प्राप्तः संप्रहृष्टतनूरुहः ..
राक्षसानां वधं कृत्वा लब्ध्वा देहं पुरातनम् .. 67 ..
5.53.m: Then, with the hair of his body bristling with joy, / having killed the rakshasas and regained his former body, he reached his city.

5.53.s:
tatastaṃ tejasā hīnaṃ durgaṃdhena samāvṛtam ..
brahmahatyodbhavaiścihnairanyairapi pṛthagvidhaiḥ .. 68 ..
5.53.d:
ततस्तं तेजसा हीनं दुर्गंधेन समावृतम् ..
ब्रह्महत्योद्भवैश्चिह्नैरन्यैरपि पृथग्विधैः .. 68 ..
5.53.m: Then, [seeing] him devoid of radiance and covered in a foul stench, / with marks born of the murder of a brahmin and other diverse kinds,

5.53.s:
dṛṣṭvā te maṃtriṇastasya putra pautrāstathā pare ..
nopasarpaṃti bhūpālaṃ pāpasparśabhayānvitāḥ .. 69 ..
5.53.d:
दृष्ट्वा ते मंत्रिणस्तस्य पुत्र पौत्रास्तथा परे ..
नोपसर्पंति भूपालं पापस्पर्शभयान्विताः .. 69 ..
5.53.m: seeing [him thus], his ministers, sons, grandsons, and others / did not approach the king, seized with fear of touching sin.

5.53.s:
ūcuśca pārthivaśreṣṭha na tvamarhasi saṃgamam ..
kartuṃ sārdhamihāsmābhirbrahmahatyā nvito yataḥ .. 6.53.70 ..
5.53.d:
ऊचुश्च पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ न त्वमर्हसि संगमम् ..
कर्तुं सार्धमिहास्माभिर्ब्रह्महत्या न्वितो यतः .. 6.53.70 ..
5.53.m: And they said: "O best of kings, you ought not / to associate with us here, since you are accompanied by the murder of a brahmin.

5.53.s:
tasmādvasiṣṭhamāhūya prāyaścittaṃ samācara ..
aśuddhaṃ śuddhimāyāti yena gātramidaṃ tava .. 71 ..
5.53.d:
तस्माद्वसिष्ठमाहूय प्रायश्चित्तं समाचर ..
अशुद्धं शुद्धिमायाति येन गात्रमिदं तव .. 71 ..
5.53.m: Therefore, having summoned Vasiṣṭha, perform an expiation / by which this impure body of yours may attain purity."

5.53.s:
tataḥ sa pārthivastūrṇaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ munipuṃgavam ..
samāhūyābravīdvākyaṃ dūrastho vinayānvitaḥ .. 72 ..
5.53.d:
ततः स पार्थिवस्तूर्णं वसिष्ठं मुनिपुंगवम् ..
समाहूयाब्रवीद्वाक्यं दूरस्थो विनयान्वितः .. 72 ..
5.53.m: Then the king quickly summoned Vasiṣṭha, the eminent sage, / and standing at a distance, filled with humility, he spoke:

5.53.s:
tava prasādato vipra sa hato rākṣaso mayā..
muktaśāpo'smi saṃjātaḥ paraṃ śṛṇu vaco mune .. 73 ..
5.53.d:
तव प्रसादतो विप्र स हतो राक्षसो मया..
मुक्तशापोऽस्मि संजातः परं शृणु वचो मुने .. 73 ..
5.53.m: "By your grace, O brahmin, that rakshasa was slain by me, / and I have become freed from the curse; but hear my words, O sage!

5.53.s:
mama gātrātsudurgaṃdhaḥ samudgacchati sarvataḥ ..
bhārākrāṃtāni gātrāṇi sarvāṇyevācalāni ca .. 74 ..
5.53.d:
मम गात्रात्सुदुर्गंधः समुद्गच्छति सर्वतः ..
भाराक्रांतानि गात्राणि सर्वाण्येवाचलानि च .. 74 ..
5.53.m: A terrible stench rises forth from my body on all sides; / all my limbs are weighed down by heaviness and are immovable.

5.53.s:
tatkimetaddvijaśreṣṭha tejo hāniratīva me ..
maṃtriṇo'pi tathā putrā na spṛśaṃti yato'dya mām .. 75 ..
5.53.d:
तत्किमेतद्द्विजश्रेष्ठ तेजो हानिरतीव मे ..
मंत्रिणोऽपि तथा पुत्रा न स्पृशंति यतोऽद्य माम् .. 75 ..
5.53.m: So what is this, O best of brahmins? My radiance is exceedingly diminished, / since ministers and sons do not touch me today."

5.53.s:
.. vasiṣṭha uvāca .. ..
rākṣasatvaṃ prapannena tvayā pārthivasattama ..
brāhmaṇā bahavo dhvastāstathā vidhvaṃsitā makhāḥ ..
teṣāṃ tvaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha saṃspṛṣṭo brahmahatyayā .. 76 ..
5.53.d:
.. वसिष्ठ उवाच .. ..
राक्षसत्वं प्रपन्नेन त्वया पार्थिवसत्तम ..
ब्राह्मणा बहवो ध्वस्तास्तथा विध्वंसिता मखाः ..
तेषां त्वं पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ संस्पृष्टो ब्रह्महत्यया .. 76 ..
5.53.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / "When you fell into the state of a rakshasa, O best of kings, / many brahmins were destroyed by you, and sacrifices were ruined; / by their murder of a brahmin you have been touched, O best of kings."

5.53.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
tadarthaṃ dehi me vipra prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhaye ..
yena nirmuktapāpo'haṃ rājyaṃ prāpnomi cātmanaḥ .. 77 ..
5.53.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
तदर्थं देहि मे विप्र प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्धये ..
येन निर्मुक्तपापोऽहं राज्यं प्राप्नोमि चात्मनः .. 77 ..
5.53.m: The king said: / "For that purpose, O brahmin, give me an expiation for purification, / by which, freed from sin, I may regain my kingdom."

5.53.s:
.. vasiṣṭha uvāca .. ..
atrārthe tīrthayātrāṃ tvaṃ kuru pārthiva sattama ..
nirmamo nirahaṃkārastataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi .. 78 ..
5.53.d:
.. वसिष्ठ उवाच .. ..
अत्रार्थे तीर्थयात्रां त्वं कुरु पार्थिव सत्तम ..
निर्ममो निरहंकारस्ततः सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि .. 78 ..
5.53.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / "For this purpose, undertake a pilgrimage to sacred fords, O best of kings; / free from possessiveness and egoism, you will then attain accomplishment."

5.53.s:
tataḥ sa pārthivaśreṣṭhaḥ saṃyatātmā jiteṃdriyaḥ ..
prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu snānaṃ cakre samā hitaḥ .. 79 ..
5.53.d:
ततः स पार्थिवश्रेष्ठः संयतात्मा जितेंद्रियः ..
प्रयागादिषु तीर्थेषु स्नानं चक्रे समा हितः .. 79 ..
5.53.m: Then that best of kings, self-restrained with conquered senses, / attentively bathed at Prayāga and other sacred fords.

5.53.s:
na naśyati sa durgaṃdho na ca tejaḥ pravardhate ..
na kāyo laghutāṃ yāti nālasyena vimucyate .. 6.53.80 ..
5.53.d:
न नश्यति स दुर्गंधो न च तेजः प्रवर्धते ..
न कायो लघुतां याति नालस्येन विमुच्यते .. 6.53.80 ..
5.53.m: The foul stench did not vanish, nor did his radiance increase; / his body did not attain lightness, nor was it freed from lethargy.

5.53.s:
tataḥ saṃbhramamāṇaśca kadāci ddvijasattamāḥ ..
camatkārapure kṣetre snānārthaṃ samupāgataḥ .. 81 ..
5.53.d:
ततः संभ्रममाणश्च कदाचि द्द्विजसत्तमाः ..
चमत्कारपुरे क्षेत्रे स्नानार्थं समुपागतः .. 81 ..
5.53.m: Then, wandering about, O best of brahmins, / he once arrived at the sacred field Camatkārapura for the sake of bathing.

5.53.s:
suśrāṃtaḥ kṣutpipāsārto niśīthe tamasāvṛte ..
gartāyāṃ patito'kasmātpūrṇāyāṃ payasā nṛpaḥ .. 82 ..
5.53.d:
सुश्रांतः क्षुत्पिपासार्तो निशीथे तमसावृते ..
गर्तायां पतितोऽकस्मात्पूर्णायां पयसा नृपः .. 82 ..
5.53.m: Utterly exhausted, afflicted with hunger and thirst, at midnight shrouded in darkness, / the king suddenly fell into a pit full of water.

5.53.s:
kṛcchrāttato viniṣkrāṃtastīrthāttasmānmahīpatiḥ ..
yāvatpaśyati cātmānaṃ dvādaśārkasamaprabham .. 83 ..
5.53.d:
कृच्छ्रात्ततो विनिष्क्रांतस्तीर्थात्तस्मान्महीपतिः ..
यावत्पश्यति चात्मानं द्वादशार्कसमप्रभम् .. 83 ..
5.53.m: When the king emerged with difficulty from that sacred ford, / he saw himself endowed with a brilliance equal to twelve suns,

5.53.s:
durgaṃdhena parityaktaṃ sodyamaṃ laghutāṃ gatam ..
dṛṣṭvā ca ciṃtayāmāsa nūnaṃ mukto'smi pātakāt .. 84 ..
5.53.d:
दुर्गंधेन परित्यक्तं सोद्यमं लघुतां गतम् ..
दृष्ट्वा च चिंतयामास नूनं मुक्तोऽस्मि पातकात् .. 84 ..
5.53.m: freed from the foul stench, full of energy, and having attained lightness. / Seeing this, he thought: 'Surely I am freed from sin!'

5.53.s:
etasminneva kāle tu vāguvācāśarīriṇī ..
harṣayantī mahīpālaṃ vimuktaṃ brahmahatyayā ..85..
5.53.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु वागुवाचाशरीरिणी ..
हर्षयन्ती महीपालं विमुक्तं ब्रह्महत्यया ..85..
5.53.m: At that very moment, a bodiless voice spoke, / bringing joy to the king who was freed from the murder of a brahmin:

5.53.s:
vimukto'si mahārāja sāṃprataṃ pūrvapātakaiḥ ..
tīrthasyāsya prabhāvena tasmādgaccha nijaṃ gṛham.. 86 ..
5.53.d:
विमुक्तोऽसि महाराज सांप्रतं पूर्वपातकैः ..
तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावेन तस्माद्गच्छ निजं गृहम्.. 86 ..
5.53.m: "O great king, you are now freed from your previous sins / by the power of this sacred ford; therefore, go to your home!

5.53.s:
atra saṃnihito nityaṃ bhrūṇarūpeṇa śaṃkaraḥ ..
kṛṣṇapakṣe viśeṣeṇa caturdaśyāṃ mahīpate .. 87 ..
5.53.d:
अत्र संनिहितो नित्यं भ्रूणरूपेण शंकरः ..
कृष्णपक्षे विशेषेण चतुर्दश्यां महीपते .. 87 ..
5.53.m: Śaṃkara is constantly present here in the form of an embryo, / especially on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, O king.

5.53.s:
yadā prapatitaṃ liṃgaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
dvijaśāpena gartaiṣā tadānena vinirmitā .. 88 ..
5.53.d:
यदा प्रपतितं लिंगं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ..
द्विजशापेन गर्तैषा तदानेन विनिर्मिता .. 88 ..
5.53.m: When the liṅga of the god of gods, the spear-wielder, fell down / due to the curse of brahmins, this pit was made by him at that time,

5.53.s:
lajjitena svavāsārthaṃ mahadduḥkhayutena ca ..
