कार्तिकस्य सिते पक्षे स याति परमां गतिम् .. 14 ..
तथा तत्र द्विजश्रेष्ठा नरनारायणावुभौ ..
देवौ परमतेजस्वी यस्तौ पश्यति भक्तितः .. 15 ..
पूजयेच्च द्विजश्रेष्ठा द्वादश्या दिवसे स्वयम् ..
स याति परमं स्थानं जरामरणवर्जितम् .. 16 ..
तीर्थयात्राकृतारंभः कुन्तीपुत्रो धनंजयः ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे समायातो द्विजोत्तमाः .. 17 ..
दृष्ट्वा तत्पावनं क्षेत्रं तीर्थपूगप्रपूरितम्..
आदित्यं स्थापयामास प्रासादे सुमनोहरे .. 18 ..
नरनारायणौ देवौ तस्याग्रे स्थापितौ ततः ..
तथा गोवर्धनधरस्तत्र देवः प्रतिष्ठितः .. 19 ..
5.60.m:
Whoever worships him with devotion on the fourth lunar day with offerings of modakas, / is freed from all obstacles and obtains the desired fruit. / Situated there for the welfare of the lords of the twice-born, O best of the twice-born […].'
He who worships him with Atharvan mantras on the twelfth lunar day / of the bright fortnight of Kārttika goes to the supreme state. // 14
Likewise there, O best of brahmins, both gods Nara and Nārāyaṇa, / endowed with supreme splendor—he who beholds the two with devotion, // 15
and worships them himself on the twelfth day, O best of brahmins, / goes to the supreme abode, free from old age and death. // 16
Having undertaken a pilgrimage to sacred fords, Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī, / arrived at the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, O best of brahmins. // 17
Seeing that purifying sacred field filled with a multitude of sacred fords, / he installed Āditya in a very delightful temple. // 18
Then the two gods Nara and Nārāyaṇa were installed before him. / Likewise the god who lifted Mount Govardhana was consecrated there, // 19

5.60.s:
narasiṃhaṃ tathaivānyaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ ..
evaṃ saṃsthāpya kauṃteyo devagṛhasupaṃcakam .. 6.60.20 ..
tato viprānsamāhūya sarvāṃstānpurasaṃbhavān ..
provāca praṇato bhaktyā dhanaṃ dattvā supuṣkalam .. 21 ..
mayā saṃsthāpitaḥ sūryaḥ sarvarogakṣayāvahaḥ ..
tathārpitaśca yuṣmākaṃ ciṃtanīyaṃ sadaiva tu .. 22 ..
.. viprā ūcuḥ .. ..
gaccha tvaṃ pāṃḍavaśreṣṭha suviśrabdhaḥ svamālayam ..
vayaṃ sarve kariṣyāmastavaśreyo'bhivardhanam .. 23 ..
tato'rjunaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā tebhyo dattvā dhanaṃ bahu..
tānāmaṃtrya namaskṛtya jagāma svapuraṃ prati .. 24 ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ narādityasya saṃbhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ śṛṇvatāṃ pāpanāśanam .. 25 ..
5.60.d:
नरसिंहं तथैवान्यं श्रद्धया परया युतः ..
एवं संस्थाप्य कौंतेयो देवगृहसुपंचकम् .. 6.60.20 ..
ततो विप्रान्समाहूय सर्वांस्तान्पुरसंभवान् ..
प्रोवाच प्रणतो भक्त्या धनं दत्त्वा सुपुष्कलम् .. 21 ..
मया संस्थापितः सूर्यः सर्वरोगक्षयावहः ..
तथार्पितश्च युष्माकं चिंतनीयं सदैव तु .. 22 ..
.. विप्रा ऊचुः .. ..
गच्छ त्वं पांडवश्रेष्ठ सुविश्रब्धः स्वमालयम् ..
वयं सर्वे करिष्यामस्तवश्रेयोऽभिवर्धनम् .. 23 ..
ततोऽर्जुनः प्रहृष्टात्मा तेभ्यो दत्त्वा धनं बहु..
तानामंत्र्य नमस्कृत्य जगाम स्वपुरं प्रति .. 24 ..
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं नरादित्यस्य संभवम् ..
माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः शृण्वतां पापनाशनम् .. 25 ..
5.60.m:
and similarly another [deity], Narasiṃha, endowed with supreme faith. / Having thus established the excellent group of five shrines of the gods, the son of Kuntī, // 20
then summoned all those brahmins born in the city, / and having bowed down in devotion and given abundant wealth, said: // 21
“The Sun, who brings about the destruction of all diseases, has been installed by me / and entrusted to you; he should always be cared for.” // 22
The brahmins said: / “Go with full confidence to your own home, O best of the Pāṇḍavas; / we all shall promote your welfare.” // 23
Then Arjuna, delighted in heart, gave much wealth to them; / bidding them farewell and bowing down, he departed for his own city. // 24
Sūta said: / “This origin of Narāditya has all been told to you, / a māhātmya that destroys sin for those who hear it, O best of brahmins.” // 25

5.60.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye narādityamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 60 .. .. cha ..
5.60.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये नरादित्यमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम षष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 60 .. .. छ ..
5.60.m: Thus ends the sixtieth chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of Narāditya,” in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 60

5.61.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
śarmiṣṭhātīrthamityuktaṃ tvayā yacca mahāmate ..
kathaṃ jātaṃ mahābhāga kiṃprabhāvaṃ tu tadvada .. 1 ..
5.61.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
शर्मिष्ठातीर्थमित्युक्तं त्वया यच्च महामते ..
कथं जातं महाभाग किंप्रभावं तु तद्वद .. 1 ..
5.61.m: The seers said: / “The sacred ford named Śarmiṣṭhā that was mentioned by you, O wise one— / how did it arise, O fortunate one, and what is its power? Speak of that!” // 1

5.61.s:
.. sūta uvāca.. ..
āsīdrājā vṛkonāma somavaṃśa samudbhavaḥ ..
brahmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca sarvalokahite rataḥ .. 2 ..
5.61.d:
.. सूत उवाच.. ..
आसीद्राजा वृकोनाम सोमवंश समुद्भवः ..
ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च सर्वलोकहिते रतः .. 2 ..
5.61.m: Sūta said: / “There was a king named Vṛka, born in the lunar dynasty, / devoted to brahmins, offering refuge, and intent upon the welfare of all beings. // 2

5.61.s:
tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī ..
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannā pativrataparāyaṇā .. .. 3 ..
5.61.d:
तस्य भार्याऽभवत्साध्वी प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी ..
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्ना पतिव्रतपरायणा .. .. 3 ..
5.61.m: His virtuous wife was dearer [to him] than life itself, / endowed with all auspicious marks and devoted to her husband. // 3

5.61.s:
atha tasyāṃ samutpannā prāpte vayasi paścime ..
kanyakā divase prāpte sarvaśāstravigarhite .. 4 ..
5.61.d:
अथ तस्यां समुत्पन्ना प्राप्ते वयसि पश्चिमे ..
कन्यका दिवसे प्राप्ते सर्वशास्त्रविगर्हिते .. 4 ..
5.61.m: Then, when her later age had arrived, there was born of her / a girl, arriving on a day condemned by all the scriptures. // 4

5.61.s:
tata ānīya viprānsa jyotirjñānavicakṣaṇān ..
papraccha kīdṛśī kanyā mameyaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati .. 5 ..
5.61.d:
तत आनीय विप्रान्स ज्योतिर्ज्ञानविचक्षणान् ..
पप्रच्छ कीदृशी कन्या ममेयं संभविष्यति .. 5 ..
5.61.m: Thereupon, having summoned brahmins skilled in the knowledge of astrology, / he asked: ‘What kind of daughter will this one of mine turn out to be?’ // 5

5.61.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ .. ..
yā kanyā prāpnuyājjanma citrāsaṃsthe divākare ..
caṃdre vāpi caturdaśyāṃ sā bhavedviṣakanyakā .. 6 ..
5.61.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः .. ..
या कन्या प्राप्नुयाज्जन्म चित्रासंस्थे दिवाकरे ..
चंद्रे वापि चतुर्दश्यां सा भवेद्विषकन्यका .. 6 ..
5.61.m: The brahmins said: / ‘The maiden who takes birth when the sun is in Citrā, / or the moon, on the fourteenth lunar day, becomes a poison-girl. // 6

5.61.s:
yastasyāḥ pratigṛhṇāti pāṇiṃ pārthivasattama ..
ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuṃ sa prāpnoti naro dhruvam .. 7 ..
5.61.d:
यस्तस्याः प्रतिगृह्णाति पाणिं पार्थिवसत्तम ..
षण्मासाभ्यंतरे मृत्युं स प्राप्नोति नरो ध्रुवम् .. 7 ..
5.61.m: The man who takes her hand [in marriage], O best of kings, / surely meets death within six months. // 7

5.61.s:
yasminsā jāyate harmye ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare ca tat ..
karoti vibhavairhīnaṃ dhanadasyāpyasaṃśayam .. 8 ..
5.61.d:
यस्मिन्सा जायते हर्म्ये षण्मासाभ्यंतरे च तत् ..
करोति विभवैर्हीनं धनदस्याप्यसंशयम् .. 8 ..
5.61.m: And the palace in which she is born, within six months / she deprives of riches, even [if it belongs] to Kubera, without a doubt. // 8

5.61.s:
seyaṃ tava sutā rājanyathoktā viṣa kanyakā ..
paitṛkaṃ śvāśurīyaṃ ca haniṣyati gṛhadvayam .. 9 ..
5.61.d:
सेयं तव सुता राजन्यथोक्ता विष कन्यका ..
पैतृकं श्वाशुरीयं च हनिष्यति गृहद्वयम् .. 9 ..
5.61.m: This daughter of yours, O king, as described, is a poison-girl; / she will destroy both families, that of her father and that of her father-in-law. // 9

5.61.s:
tasmādimāṃ parityajya sukhī bhava narādhipa ..
śraddadhāsi vaco'smākaṃ hita muktaṃ yadi prabho .. 6.61.10 ..
5.61.d:
तस्मादिमां परित्यज्य सुखी भव नराधिप ..
श्रद्दधासि वचोऽस्माकं हित मुक्तं यदि प्रभो .. 6.61.10 ..
5.61.m: Therefore, abandon her and be happy, O lord of men, / if you trust our word, which is spoken for your welfare, O master.’ // 10

5.61.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
tyakṣyāmi yadi nāmaitāṃ dhārayiṣyāmi vā gṛhe ..
anyadehodbhavaṃ karma phaliṣyati tathāpi me .. 11 ..
5.61.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
त्यक्ष्यामि यदि नामैतां धारयिष्यामि वा गृहे ..
अन्यदेहोद्भवं कर्म फलिष्यति तथापि मे .. 11 ..
5.61.m: The king said: / ‘Whether I abandon her or keep her in my house, / the action born of another body will still bear fruit for me. // 11

5.61.s:
śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ na tu śakyaṃ prarakṣitum ..
tasmātkarma puraskṛtya naiva tyakṣyāmi kanyakām .. 12 ..
5.61.d:
शुभं वा यदि वा पापं न तु शक्यं प्ररक्षितुम् ..
तस्मात्कर्म पुरस्कृत्य नैव त्यक्ष्यामि कन्यकाम् .. 12 ..
5.61.m: Whether good or evil, it is not possible to avert it. / Therefore, placing karma first, I shall not abandon my daughter. // 12

5.61.s:
yenayena śarīreṇa yadyatkarma karoti yaḥ ..
tenatenaiva bhūyaḥ sa prāpnoti sakalaṃ phalam .. 13 ..
5.61.d:
येनयेन शरीरेण यद्यत्कर्म करोति यः ..
तेनतेनैव भूयः स प्राप्नोति सकलं फलम् .. 13 ..
5.61.m: With whichever body one performs whatever action, / with that very [body] he receives back its full fruit. // 13

5.61.s:
yasyāṃ yasyāmavasthāyāṃ kriyate'tra śubhāśubham ..
tasyāṃ tasyāṃ dhruvaṃ tasya phalaṃ tadbhujyate naraiḥ .. 14 ..
5.61.d:
यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां क्रियतेऽत्र शुभाशुभम् ..
तस्यां तस्यां ध्रुवं तस्य फलं तद्भुज्यते नरैः .. 14 ..
5.61.m: In whatever state good or bad is done here, / in that very state its fruit is surely experienced by men. // 14

5.61.s:
na naśyati purākarma kṛtaṃ sarveṃdriyairiha ..
akṛtaṃ jāyate naiva tasmānnāsti bhayaṃ mama .. 15 ..
5.61.d:
न नश्यति पुराकर्म कृतं सर्वेंद्रियैरिह ..
अकृतं जायते नैव तस्मान्नास्ति भयं मम .. 15 ..
5.61.m: Past action performed here with all the sense organs does not perish, / nor does what is not done come into being; therefore I have no fear. // 15

5.61.s:
āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanameva ca ..
pañcaitāni hi sṛjyante garbhasthasyaiva dehinaḥ .. 16 ..
5.61.d:
आयुः कर्म च वित्तं च विद्या निधनमेव च ..
पञ्चैतानि हि सृज्यन्ते गर्भस्थस्यैव देहिनः .. 16 ..
5.61.m: Lifespan, karma, wealth, learning, and death itself— / these five are indeed created for an embodied being while still in the womb. // 16

5.61.s:
yathā vṛkṣeṣu vallīṣu kusumāni phalāni ca ..
svakālaṃ nātivartaṃte tadvatkarma purākṛtam .. 17 ..
5.61.d:
यथा वृक्षेषु वल्लीषु कुसुमानि फलानि च ..
स्वकालं नातिवर्तंते तद्वत्कर्म पुराकृतम् .. 17 ..
5.61.m: Just as flowers and fruits on trees and creepers / do not exceed their own proper season, so it is with past karma. // 17

5.61.s:
yenaiva yadyathā pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ karma śubhāśubham ..
sa eva tattathā bhuṃkte nityaṃ vihitamātmanaḥ .. 18 ..
5.61.d:
येनैव यद्यथा पूर्वं कृतं कर्म शुभाशुभम् ..
स एव तत्तथा भुंक्ते नित्यं विहितमात्मनः .. 18 ..
5.61.m: Just as whatever action, good or evil, was performed by someone previously, / he alone experiences it in that manner, as ordained for himself forever. // 18

5.61.s:
yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram ..
tathaivaṃ koṭimadhyasthaṃ kartāraṃ karma vindati .. 19 ..
5.61.d:
यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् ..
तथैवं कोटिमध्यस्थं कर्तारं कर्म विन्दति .. 19 ..
5.61.m: Just as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, / so karma finds the agent even in the midst of ten million [beings]. // 19

5.61.s:
anyadehakṛtaṃ karma na kaścitpuruṣo bhuvi ..
balena prajñayā vāpi samarthaḥ kartumanyathā .. 6.61.20 ..
5.61.d:
अन्यदेहकृतं कर्म न कश्चित्पुरुषो भुवि ..
बलेन प्रज्ञया वापि समर्थः कर्तुमन्यथा .. 6.61.20 ..
5.61.m: Karma done in another body, no person on earth / is able to alter by force or by intellect. // 20

5.61.s:
anyathā śāstragarbhiṇyā dhiyā dhīro mahīyate ..
svāmivatprākkṛtaṃ karma vidadhāti tadanyathā .. 21 ..
5.61.d:
अन्यथा शास्त्रगर्भिण्या धिया धीरो महीयते ..
स्वामिवत्प्राक्कृतं कर्म विदधाति तदन्यथा .. 21 ..
5.61.m: Otherwise, a wise man, distinguished with an intellect rich in the scriptures, / is made to act differently by past karma acting like a master. // 21

5.61.s:
svakṛtānyupatiṣṭhaṃti sukhaduḥkhāni dehinām ..
hetubhūto hi yasteṣāṃ so'haṃkāreṇa badhyate .. 22 ..
5.61.d:
स्वकृतान्युपतिष्ठंति सुखदुःखानि देहिनाम् ..
हेतुभूतो हि यस्तेषां सोऽहंकारेण बध्यते .. 22 ..
5.61.m: The joys and sorrows of embodied beings that approach them are their own doing; / for he who considers himself the cause of them is bound by egoism. // 22

5.61.s:
suśīghramabhidhāvantaṃ nijaṃ karmānudhāvati ..
śete saha śayānena tiṣṭhantamanutiṣṭhati .. 23 ..
5.61.d:
सुशीघ्रमभिधावन्तं निजं कर्मानुधावति ..
शेते सह शयानेन तिष्ठन्तमनुतिष्ठति .. 23 ..
5.61.m: One's own karma runs after him as he runs very swiftly; / it lies down with him as he sleeps, and it stands beside him as he stands. // 23

5.61.s:
yathā chāyātapau nityaṃ susaṃbaddhau parasparam ..
tathā karma ca kartā ca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 29 ..
yena yatropabhoktavyaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhameva vā ..
naraḥ sa baddho rajjveva balāttatraiva nīyate .. 25 ..
pramāṇaṃ karmabhūtānāṃ sukhaduḥkhopapādane ..
sāvadhānatayā yacca jāgratāṃ svapatāmapi .. 26 ..
tailakṣaye yathā dīpo nirvāṇamadhigacchati ..
karmakṣaye tathā jaṃturnirvāṇamadhigacchati .. 27 ..
na mantrā na tapo dānaṃ na tīrthaṃ na ca saṃyamaḥ ..
samarthā rakṣituṃ jaṃtuṃ pīḍitaṃ pūrvakarmabhiḥ .. 28 ..
saṃgatyā jaṭhare nyasto retobinduracetanaḥ ..
ṛtukāle manuṣyeṇa vṛddhiṃ gacchati karmataḥ .. 29 ..
5.61.d:
यथा छायातपौ नित्यं सुसंबद्धौ परस्परम् ..
तथा कर्म च कर्ता च नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 29 ..
येन यत्रोपभोक्तव्यं सुखं वा दुःखमेव वा ..
नरः स बद्धो रज्ज्वेव बलात्तत्रैव नीयते .. 25 ..
प्रमाणं कर्मभूतानां सुखदुःखोपपादने ..
सावधानतया यच्च जाग्रतां स्वपतामपि .. 26 ..
तैलक्षये यथा दीपो निर्वाणमधिगच्छति ..
कर्मक्षये तथा जंतुर्निर्वाणमधिगच्छति .. 27 ..
न मन्त्रा न तपो दानं न तीर्थं न च संयमः ..
समर्था रक्षितुं जंतुं पीडितं पूर्वकर्मभिः .. 28 ..
संगत्या जठरे न्यस्तो रेतोबिन्दुरचेतनः ..
ऋतुकाले मनुष्येण वृद्धिं गच्छति कर्मतः .. 29 ..
5.61.m:
Just as shadow and sunlight are always closely connected to each other, / so are karma and the agent; no doubt should be entertained here. // 24
Where and by whom pleasure or pain is to be experienced, / that person, as if bound by a rope, is forcibly led to that very place. // 25
Karma is the authoritative measure for living beings in bringing about pleasure and pain, / as well as attentiveness for those who are awake and those who sleep. // 26
Just as a lamp goes out when its oil is exhausted, / so a creature attains extinction when its karma is exhausted. // 27
Neither mantras, nor austerity, nor gifts, nor a sacred ford, nor self-restraint / are capable of protecting a creature afflicted by past karma. // 28
The insentient drop of semen deposited in the womb through intercourse / by a man in the fertile season grows on account of karma. // 29

5.61.s:
annapānāni jīryaṃti yatra bhakṣyaṃ ca bhakṣitam ..
tasminnevodare garbhaḥ kathaṃ nāma na jīryati .. 6.61.30 ..
5.61.d:
अन्नपानानि जीर्यंति यत्र भक्ष्यं च भक्षितम् ..
तस्मिन्नेवोदरे गर्भः कथं नाम न जीर्यति .. 6.61.30 ..
5.61.m: Where food and drink are digested, along with whatever has been eaten, / in that very belly, how does the embryo not digest?

5.61.s:
tasmātkarmakṛtaṃ sarvaṃ dehināmatra jāyate ..
śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpamiti me niścayaḥ sadā .. 31 ..
5.61.d:
तस्मात्कर्मकृतं सर्वं देहिनामत्र जायते ..
शुभं वा यदि वा पापमिति मे निश्चयः सदा .. 31 ..
5.61.m: Therefore, everything that befalls embodied beings here is produced by their actions, / whether good or whether sin: this is my firm conviction always.

5.61.s:
arakṣitaṃ tiṣṭhati daivarakṣitaṃ surakṣitaṃ daivahataṃ vinaśyati ..
jīvatyanātho'pi vane visarjitaḥ kṛtaprayatno'pi gṛhe na jīvati .. 32 ..
5.61.d:
अरक्षितं तिष्ठति दैवरक्षितं सुरक्षितं दैवहतं विनश्यति ..
जीवत्यनाथोऽपि वने विसर्जितः कृतप्रयत्नोऽपि गृहे न जीवति .. 32 ..
5.61.m: The unprotected survives if protected by fate; the well-protected perishes if struck by fate. / Even abandoned in the forest, one without a protector lives; even after great effort is made, one does not live at home.

5.61.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye viṣakanyakotpattivarṇanaṃnāmaikaṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 61 ..
5.61.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये विषकन्यकोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनामैकषष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 61 ..
5.61.m: Thus ends the sixty-first chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the Poison-Maiden,' in the Māhātmya of the Holy Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the sixth [section], the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
